Preface:
The more I think about this game, the more utterly angry I get. The developers of this game, Chucklefish, got 4 million dollars in half pre orders, half kickstarter PLUS an early access which did 1 million sales initially at $14.99 a pop and 3 years 5 months from start of development to now and this game is STILL in alpha. This is scandalous. This is litigious. Because they weren't short on time or money and let's face it, it's a ♥♥♥♥ing procedurally generated 2-D sidescroller. They haven't worked on anything but minor bug fixes and superfluous mechanics and artwork for a long, long time. The topping is this game is far from complete.
This unfinished game which currently has incredibly dull gameplay, shows no sign of completion any time soon. And at the end of the day, even if it is finished it's probably going to feel as the game it is now. Dull, dry, monotonous. The height of tedium, from building to combat to mining to questing. Every facet of this game is incredibly droll and boring, and I will go into further detail in the actual review segment.
Bottom line:
$4,000,000 in pre orders. According to SteamSpy, there are roughly 1,891,483 owners of Starbound. Assuming Steam takes a 30% cut, then approximately $19,000,000 in profit.
So in 3 years, 6 months and profits of 23 MILLION DOLLARS can not get this game complete.
Houses in the Bahamas, off shore bank accounts. Which would be perfectly fine if the developers were competent game makers and made a polished, complete product in a reasonable timeframe. They are not and they did not.
This company is either incompetent or conmen. I'd seriously advise against buying this product and view every game this company develops in the future with avid skeptism.
Review:
Starbound is an open ended galactic themed 2D sandbox game heavily based off the very successful Terraria. But this is also a sad tale of disappointment that profits off the good intentions of the consumer supporting the underdog indie developer.
You start the game with a tool that allows you to mine at a very slow pace. This device can be upgraded, but only by use of rare loot based drops. And with each upgrade you need more of this rare item. The game excruciating hands out mining progression, which is a running theme.
This is one of those games where building absolutely does not matter... That's it. Building any structures is pointless. I would argue this would be a game of creativity, but you have to unlock schematics in order to get access of cosmetic objects, and these are unlocked at an excruciatingly slow rate.
The combat is dry. Quite simply because this is not a survival game. At a time you will have three mobs on the screen, half of which will not be hostile and winning is based more on the tier of your equipment than any meaningful combat decision making.
Quest Progression In It's Entirety:
Mine tier 1 ore -> Make tier 1 equipment -> Complete tier 1 quest -> Mine tier 2 ore -> Make tier 2 equipment -> Complete tier 2 quest -> Mine tier 3 ore -> Make tier 3 equipment -> Complete tier 3 quest -> Mine tier 4 ore -> Make tier 4 equipment -> Complete tier 4 quest -> Mine tier 5 ore -> Make tier 5 equipment -> Complete tier 5 quest....
(This is literally what the quest system is. Developer has nothing but contempt for audience.)
I can't wait for them to finish this game so I can ♥♥♥♥ing do the same ♥♥♥♥ing thing again and again and again with absolutely no excitement. Then I can just ♥♥♥♥ing kill myself.
And what are the main quests? Mostly a dull gauntlet run to a boss which. Don't be fooled, that makes it sound better than it is. It's wandering through a multiple path procedurally generated environment filled with enemies which more often than not becomes a battle of attrition due to the fact you're just wandering the same rooms which no sense of direction coupled with how you start to inadvertently soak damage because of how dry and monotonous it is. To be fair, the bosses themselves can be moderately challenging as they have patterns that must be adapted to but they are still♥♥♥♥♥♥easy. If you die the first time you'll win the second.
What about side missions? Someone needs a cake for no reason, your reward is a weapon that is worse than anything you can craft. Oh boy that was fun. One wanted me to give them a vanity item in exchange for another vanity item and that was my reward.
Now this is the most glaring and obvious criticism most players bring up without actively targeting. The established universe is subject to development whims and not subject to any form of grounding, especially when this doesn't factor into any form of gameplay. This is a problem. Having a space terraria style sandbox, but still digging through the mud with a pickaxe and using rusty swords is the biggest bait and switch I've ever heard.
Everything in the Starbound universe is a joke or reference or whacky in nature with absolutely no grounding, so you are incapable of being invested. Why should you care? The game doesn't. The races are a joke, settlements are a joke, quests are a joke. And they're all bad jokes in the Douglas Adams vein. The game goes to such length to show how it doesn't take itself seriously at all, but there is no payoff.
This is the video game equivalent of someone handing you a bad finger painting and saying "Here's my bad finger painting! Look at how bad it is!" expecting you to laugh. How are we meant to respond? "Hahahahahaha! You don't care at all and I paid you for this! I guess the jokes on me! Haha... ha... ha...."
You can have a joke game but you need actual jokes. When Chucklefish's idea of a joke is making fun of their own flat universe... Jesus christ, really? Could you have more contempt for your audience and more self awareness?
Long story short, it's Terraria but worse. Much worse. Technically it has more "content" but the whole game is dry and dull, dry and dull.
Essentially a sprite artist from Re-Logic (creators of Terraria) remade a subpar, stagnating Terraria and made millions and consumers are torn between lynch mob and white knights.
The only thing I can say to this games defence is it has a lot of pixel graphic assets (oh very taxing) and it's music is good.
This company is fascinatingly cynical, because no aspect is fleshed out and it's not even a focus.
"I'd really love to see some more games made on the Starbound engine, its so flexible and easy" - Tiy Jun 27 - 2015
Do you know what this says to me?
"We ♥♥♥♥ed up. We don't know what we're doing. Someone please make a good game for us. All we can do is make innocuous content."
I resent this company, for being the most obviously cynical cash grab bare bones example of a game completely supported by hype, false promises and implications.
We have enough problems with EA, Ubisoft, Warner Brothers without ambitious little ♥♥♥♥♥ doing it as well.
PS. Hey Tiy, I don't think you were meant to use the millions of dollars you got to start a publishing business... Pretty sure it was to just make a game.
Note: I edit this review frequently to better express my supreme disappointment of this title and to convey that Chucklefish are as trustworthy as EA.

Despite the title, Mad Games Tycoon has no correlation to the other Mad game, Tv Tycoon, despite both games sharing a very eerily similar title. The devs deny it but can't help question the likeness. Regardless, Mad Games Tycoon has more in common with Game Dev Tycoon, except that MGT is more indepth and has a lot more too it.
Already as an early access title, its got enough features to keep you entertained. Where as Game Dev Tycoon is more of a mobile type of game, and rather simple in design, Mad is designed to be more PC worthy in that it has a lot more features such as running your own production machines, storage and servers for online games that you have to setup. You also have to setup a support team for technical support, and keep your dev team happy and productive with amenities dotted abuot the office. Although I've yet to see any direct consequences of NOT having stuff around to keep your employee morale up, it may become more prominent later on.
There's also the fact that you can essentially build your own office and place things where you need them. Mad Games Tycoon definitely reminds me of an old PC game called 'Startup' that had a lot of these features, but in the end was a very poor implementation. MGT seems to have gotten it right, so far at least.
Their are a few shortfalls however that the game lacks that I hope the devs work on in the future, this including staff categories and perhaps a more immersive background experience, perhaps a road and some animated cars/people walking by including all the noise that comes with that?
I'm also not sure if modding features are ever going to be supported, but hopefully they will.
Regardless, if you liked Game Dev Tycoon, or even, if you didn't like it and thought it was too simple, then I can recommend this as so far its a great title, and it looks to improve even more in the near future.

NEW PATCH IS A NEW WHOLE KILLER GAME REBOOT!
The Original Version of //N.P.P.D. RUSH// blew the mind out of my head, removed my limbs, and tossed me into the hyper-real clusterf##k of patterns and surreal violence that is Nauseous Pines. Now, MHLK 2.0 is Back TO KILL MY BODY.
My first impression of RUSH was like taking a hit of:
ENTER THE VOID, ROBOCOP, NAKED LUNCH, VIDEODROME, AND/OR BRAZIL while playing a glitched out SEGA Death.
It was a thrilling, desperate, intensely stimulating, and sickening ride. The visuals, sexy, tiled, and multi-textured, made me feel like I was bolting through a cramped, neon and chippy glass tower of 198X excess. The parallax scrolling and layering effects gave off the weirdest sense of dimensional overwhelm. The details beg for careful observation and some kind of meaning, but there are urgent matters pulling you into the search for bodies. Memory strategies and knowledge are gained through your failures and experiments, and it all starts to make sense and click in the end. A tense pulling apart of the mind's pattern recognition software is ultimately required to reach and defeat Ultraviolet. The classic version can be found on Desura service for those that crave it's crazy charm.
UPDATE IS LIKE SUPER HARD AWESOME MODE GAME:
Installing the new version makes RUSH a totally revamped and extremely arcade like experience. You go way faster, hear louder music and more of it, kill more, face a more coherent and solidified challenge, and easily access upgrade shops from the start of each floor. You get brand new level designs, new graphics, new enemies and game mechanics, new presentation of ideas, and a new level of challenge. If you were perhaps turned off by the charming and quirky but problematic roughness features in the previous version, you will be happy to see that there is now a standard fullscreen mode, intro, menu screen, options and effect settings. When you die, you can start again without repeating the intro text. The new RUSH is a like a hardcore challenge mode. While the pre-patch version seemed to focus more on the mood, aesthetics and weirdness, the updated game focuses on action, speed running, and a smooth bullet hell gameplay experience. There is far less clutter and confusion, and more raw violence. The added CRT monitor, fatchip, and scanline effects are cool, but unfortunately I had to disable them by running in windows xp compatibility mode for my old rig to play without lag (Try running in 256 Color mode for an OLD TIMEY DOS feeling :) Overall, I feel the two versions are almost different games. Each with a different kind of charm and appeal to it. I have yet to succeed in completing my mission in the new version, It really is fare and challenging, I just suck. I recommend you play and master this game with me.

Okay, I'm going to do something crazy and still recommend this game (when on sale!) despite everything. Despite the game being unfinished, despite the odds of any further progress on the game being extremely unlikely.
Why, you ask? Because there is still a lot of fun to be had here. If you take a close look at the negative reviews they are (understandably) because game development has ceased, not because they hated the core gameplay aspects.
I really enjoy the atmosphere in this game. It feels a lot like a single player Terraria with a focus on a dark atmosphere and an interesting story (such as it is). Carving out a small place of safety in a harsh and outright malicious world is very satisfying, along with slowly but surely improving one's tech tree and equipment in order to be able to explore harsher areas and recover tiny tidybits about those who came before you and what happened to them.
It really is a shame this game was never completed, but there is still a lot of gameplay available to those willing to give it a try. I wouldn't ask people to pay $15 for this unless they REALLY like these kinds of games, but if you see this on sale I would give it some real consideration.

Indie game, N.P.P.D RUSH - The milk of Ultraviolet, tries it's best to bring retro arcade style goodness to the Steam storefront with it's top down shooter gameplay and maze like level exploration, but unfortunately it falls short in a number of areas.  Even with the low cost of entry and the fact that it is currently on sale for 20% off as a new release, N.P.P.D does little to innovate in a genre that has been inspired by a plethora of other indie games as of late.  The look and feel are straight out of the mid-to-late 80's, but the gameplay unfortunately doesn't live up to the expectations or the intuitive mechanics we've come to enjoy from other modern classics such as Retro City Rampage or Hotline Miami.  If you're feeling nostalgic then you'd be better off saving your money for one of those two titles rather than picking up N.P.P.D RUSH in it's current form.  The gameplay sounds interesting on paper, but is only interesting for brief periods of time and coffee break style playthrus.  In fact it's very hard to categorize or compare the gameplay when it feels like a combination of less complete versions of more popular games and arcade gameplay styles.
The lack of any leaderboards, steam acheivements, or trading cards is unfortunate because those things might give gamers extra incentive to return to the game.  The complete lack of an options menu and the fact that there is
is also very disappointing considering that these extra features should be seen as a fundamental inclusion for any and all Arcade style games, top-down shooters, and of course platformers, whether it's an independently developed game or not, and
.  This is the year 2014 after all.
Here are the pros and cons:
- Interesting neon graphic style.  Very flashy, much like the arcade games of yesteryear.
- Oldschool gameplay, reminiscent of the old Arcade games, Amiga games, Commadore, and Apple games.
- Keyboard and mouse controls are fairly responsive, while also barely forgiveable.
- Gameplay *can* be fun, but only in short bursts.
- The graphics might be a hit or miss for some gamers.  You'll either appreciate the aesthetics or absolutely hate them.
- The music isn't very memorable and can become quite repetitive and annoying after a short time.
-  Extremely basic user interface.
-  No options menu.  **
**
-
This is an absolute must for any and all arcade style games or platformers these days.
-  Nostalgia can only get you so far.  I appreciate the effort, but the entertainment value here is limited.
For now I'd have to say pass this one up.  With a little luck, maybe N.P.P.D will have an update or two that will rectify it's problems and glaring omissions.  If you're in the mood for retro arcade style goodness then check out Retro City Rampage, Hotline Miami, Aqua Kitty, Love, Oniken, or Muri, all of which can be found here on Steam.  You'll get much more value for your dollar out of them.

X-blades tells a tale of a brash treasure hunter, Ayumi, whose lack of caution brings her trouble when she steals an artifact from a temple. After experiencing the effects of the artifact's curse, the protagonist is somehow transported onto the beach of some ruins and from there she makes her way through the ruins. After three to four hours of playing, I have dropped the game as I haven't seen much good in what I have experienced.
First, the voice of the protagonist is kind of grating in a bratty way. I think the intent for the character was for her to be absolutely sure of her abilities, as in "I'm the greatest treasure hunter in the world," but the voice doesn't pair well with Ayumi who shows disregard for caution. Instead of exuding confidence, when she publically makes this claim, it makes her come off as an immature kid which makes it hard to take her seriously. Maybe she gets better later in the story, but the rest of the game isn't good enough to compel me to continue.
Second, the basic aerial sword combat is unsatisfying. While on the ground, her swinging of her sword and contacting enemies feels alright. Her jumping, however, is very floaty which makes air combat strange to execute against aerial monsters. It is difficult to quickly determine how many hits that are launched are actually damaging the enemies or whether she's just floating and waving her swords around, especially when the camera angle is not facing the enemies. Considering that swordplay against enemies is the main way of building up a rage meter that is used for launching spells, improvement in this would have made a major contribution in making the game better.
This lackluster air sword combat then ties into her heavy dependence on long-ranged skills and guns to attack aerial monsters. The problem is that the pistols take at least a few shots to bring down one enemy, assuming that the enemy isn't an elemental type that's immune to physical damage, and spells require rage to use, which builds up very slowly when using her guns. Ayumi can technically charge up rage while standing still and pressing the appropriate button but then she becomes an easier target for enemies. Not only that, but rage depletes over time, so she can build up rage for a short moment and then have to flee, whereupon she starts to lose rage. The alternative way is to get hit by enemies which allows her to quickly build range and launch spells but then she can only take so much damage before she dies. I think the frustration with this is a bit evident based on how having an unsatisfying air sword combat results in having to rely on long-range attacks that most of the time can be equally disappointing.
Now having a poor air sword combat and long-range attacks would not be as big of a deal if there were few aerial monsters. Unfortunately, these type of enemies occur quite frequently and very commonly in groups which makes them the most annoying enemies to deal with. Elemental aerial types are even worse if there are more than a few of them, especially if the player didn't purchase the correct spells to deal with their elemental weakness.
Another part that bothered me is the pricing of the spells and its related issues. To purchase spells, Ayumi has to collect souls, either by defeating enemies or destroying destructible objects such as statues, and she can earn spells at a faster rate by continuously hitting enemies with her swords without taking damage whereupon a multiplier with its value dependent on the number of attacks successfully executed. The beginning spells seem to be priced reasonably, but after the first few purchases, the pricing seem to sky rocket all over the place and with each spell purchase the subsequent spell can cost on the scale of ten times more. So how does this become a problem?  If a player commits to buying some pricy spells, it can bite them back when facing off against a mini-boss or boss who can be defeated much easier with spells that weren't purchased.  The player might not even be good enough and will die repeatedly, and if the person is only relying on auto-save for his game, he's going to be respawning and repeatedly fighting the same boss because the game loads from the beginning of the level. And the soul multiplier? That is actually useful against enemies on the ground but pretty much useless against aerial enemies who are more likely to get a hit onto a Ayumi every time she attempts air combat.
Lastly, the plot is too haphazard.  The plot starts off relatively well with background on the main character and the disaster she gets herself into for taking the artifact, but after entering the ruins on the beach, it feels like it falls on the wayside as the game transitions into a repetition of entering a level, wiping the enemies, and going onto the next level. Cutscenes occasionally occur but the transitions into them are abrupt. There is a lack of continuity which makes if feel like plot points are suddenly tacked on to give a semblance of a story and that is disappointing given the start of the game.
Having said all of the negatives, there are a few positives that can be said about this game. The environments are interesting and well-varied. They're not particularly sophisticated in level design but are nice to look at and show the ambition of the developer in terms of environmental design. Although stylistically different, the cutscenes are great and fluid, showing off the anime style very well. The game looks great, but I wish the rest of the game matched the style of the cutscenes although I imagine that would be hard to pull off.  Ayumi's AOE spells are satisfying to use as they give a distinct visual impact when execute, in contrast to the lackluster basic combat.
Overall, I can't really recommend the game unless you're a huge fan of the hack-and-slash genre and are scraping the bottom of the barrel. You're much better off playing the spiritual successor, Blades of Time, which improves on all aspects of the game.

Before I tell my Review of Fallout 4, let me tell you that I have hundreds upon hundreds of hours of Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas, including atleast a hundred hours on Fallout 4 on console. Fallout 3 and New Vegas are the true Fallout games with its story telling and RPG elements, unlike Fallout 4. But... Does that make it a bad game? No.

Fallout 4 is a shooter game with tons of building mechanics ranging from weapons, armor, power armor and even settlements that you can construct bases and forts with your ideas. Many places to explore and find new loot, including enemies and locations that are interesting with some mystery, which leads to curiosity to the player's mind.  Those are the strong suits of fallout 4. Fallout 3 and New Vegas didn't have the best combat systems, nor the best building system. Fallout 4 succeeds with these mechanics greatly. Combat feels nice and smooth, building can take up hours of your time like deciding what your gun should have on or what you want on your armor, or even on your beast of a suit... Power armor. But the best part is building your settlement. Build a place from you own ideas of what makes your home you! Or building a town or multiple towns of all your liking. Make building a reason for. Add a Saloon, trade shop, homes for your people, armory and even a arena for entertainment. GO WILD! There's more then 30 places to build whatever! But you can't just stay inside a base for too long. No you gotta explore Boston and all of its riches seeing all sorts of enemies and areas! Find companions to help aid your travels with their own personality of their story and some unique dialogues to the many of places you explore. Enjoy the combat and the feel for scavenging new weapons and junk for your settlements. Every weapon you pick up can be your pride and joy. Use mods to seek your purpose for you weapon and name it whatever you see fit. Look at landmarks that Boston has to offer and find locations that are hidden with a bit of story. Ranging from terminals from the raiders you just killed and notes and recordings that show what happen to that complete skeleton that lying on the floor in front of you. Its a world that is filled with weapons, loot and some story. (Not as much story as Fallout 3 and New Vegas of course but its still there) It's up to you to explore, hunt, loot and build whatever you want. You just have to enjoy what it is. But of course there are some drawbacks.
Now Fallout 4 was a dissapointment for alot of people. The reason was that it wasn't really a RPG, but just a shooter. I was one of them, the quests were all dumbed down, less decisions to make and the lack of your creation to symbolize your character how you wanted it to be... But I did try out Fallout 4 on PC because I really love mouse and keyboard, the graphics was dumbed down but I didnt mind. I threw all comparions of Fallout New Vegas and 4 out the Window and enjoyed Fallout 4 as it is. A Shooter with fun building mechanics and great exploration of areas and loot. I did not expect an RPG. I expected a Shooter. With all that in mind, I enjoyed the game again, enjoyed it ALOT. It was fun. Every fight was great. Every area to explore was great and the thrill of excitement when you find a weapon you wanted or finding alot of precious junk that you need for your building needs feels so good. Its so satifying  to explore new areas with new enemies with new weapons and armor, and if you are lucky enough, you can find Legendary enemies that carry special unique variets of effects, and there are A TON of effects to weapons and armor, some are amazing, some are bad and some are just plain funny, you can find a walking cane that can cripple people (The irony) or have a fatman that can LITERALLY SHOOT 10 MINENUKES ALL AT THE SAME TIME WITH THE RIGHT MODS! There are endless effects for endless guns with endless mods! You can mod them to whatever you like! You can use em! Prestion can use em( If he isnt bothering you about settlements) and even your supermutant friend can use em! WEAPONS UPON MORE WEAPONS! Be a tank with armor or be a sneaky ninja with mods! You can make a pistol an LMG if you wanted too!(Pipe Pistol) Build a fort that anything unfriendly gets obliterated due to how much weapons you and your settlers have. The giant vast world makes exploring fun and enjoyable, never knowing what legendary gear, bobbleheads, junk or that shiny new gun that you've been looking for until you start exploring, even if you have to fight to the death for it! Luckily for you, this game has a great combat system!
Also the whole paid mods thing is kinda bad but when I heard about it I thought all the player made mods in the game would all be deleted. But seeing how it still up and running it was a sign of relief and I didnt see much of a problem with this situation, all the really good mods are for free. All the paid mods are ok. If you dont like it, dont buy it.
Conclusion:
Most people don't like Fallout 4 because it really doesn't have any RPG elements that carry over to the older games. Which is very true. I hated this game because it wasn't a RPG. People tend to hate sequels because people compare older greater games to newer sequel games that seem bad compared to the others. The same thing can happen for pretty much anything in life. Movies, books, etc. If Fallout 4 wasnt a fallout game, it would be a huge success. But carrying the Fallout name, it gets its hate. To make the game enjoyable to play, throw away the hate of it not being an RPG and just accept it as a shooter, building, free roam game.
If you don't.... You'll forever hate it and will be doomed.

If you, like me, are totally new even to the board game Blood Bowl, this might be a tricky one. There's alot of rules to consider, and the tutorial, while enjoyably short, doesn't give you anything else except the most basic parts. Going from that into the regular game is quite a challenge.
That being said, as a digital tactical board game, this one is really good. I've been considering this or BB2 for a while, and eventually decided to pick this one up on sale. If you're really new to this kind of game or specifically Blood Bowl, that might be the way to go, since poor understanding how the game plays out will see you soundly beaten in the beginning. It will take a couple of hours just to get the understanding needed to actually achieve something, and if you're new to this and don't have that kind of patience, this might be something to let go.
However, once the bits and pieces come together, it actually makes alot of sense, and the game plays out really well. There's some RNG involved since alot of actions, tackles, passes etc are made with dice, but there's nothing unexpected here, wich means that if you have a better than average chance of success, you're more likely to succeed than not. Of course, messing up and ending up completely trust the dice rolls, you're going to get into trouble, but as long as you have a valid tactic and execute, you have a good chance of winning games.
Tactics is very important, and shouldn't be underestimated, and you'd do well to choose your lineup depending on your preferred playing style. If you want to go physical, don't pick light and fast units f.x, and if you want to play a passing game (wich really can be beautiful), pick a line for that with quick units that are good throwers and recievers.
Even more important: if you realize you're better at another tactic than the one you actually prefer, run with what you're good at. I'd like to play a long passing game f.x, but I'm appearently most proficient with a tackle/running game, so that's what I'm going with.
All in all, if you have the patience to get into the game, this will give you alot of good gaming time. For a tactical board gamer I'd say this is a good pick, if you on top of that is a fan of Warhammer 40k this should be a must-have. Highly recommended.

I appear to be the first negative reviewer to have completed Blood Bowl in its entirety. This game has two distinct parts, the dating and the Bad Boys Love secret match unlocked by romancing every orc possible!!
The first part is simply too short to be entertaining. Any match in Blood Bowl can be played in about an hour going at a relaxed pace, but there is significant overlap between matches, including sections that have no effect on the particular match you're playing, so I found myself skipping more and more as I replayed. This also caused me to inadvertently skip content I hadn't dice rolled before, because some sections have multiple outcomes but start out the same way regardless of match. There is no way to go back to content accidentally skipped without reloading or starting a new game and it simply wasn't interesting enough to worth bothering to find out why I was faced with the choice of telling that one cute Orc with the pigtails "convenience store" or "grocery store" and I could infer it had something to do with pudding anyway.
Consequently, there just isn't enough time to give any character depth and there's no challenge to complete a match. By the time you finish a match, you feel like you were merely introduced to the team. Picking matches is also very obvious and there is never any difficulty in seducing the various orcs, unless you can't figure out that picking every opportunity to spend time with your desired orc is necessary to romance them. The matches I enjoyed most against Bonecrusher, Fister, and Anghel, stood out because they were simply the most oddball. For a game that is billed as an orc romance game, most matches utilize stereotypical melodrama. Orc puns and poop culture references abound, but there's really nothing laugh out loud funny in Blood Bowl and at best you'll smirk a lot.
All in all, Blood Bowl wasn't an altogether terrible game, but it just wasn't worth the money and I got it in a 50% off sale. I will likely never play it again and would forget about it entirely if Steam didn't keep it in my library forever. As some consolation, the sexy trading cards were surprisingly valuable and I was able to quickly sell them for about $1000.
If you don't mind a lot of repetition, love Blood Bowl no matter what, and really love silly gimmicks, then buy this game. Otherwise, pick up just about any other RnG game on Steam. Even some of the free ones are more entertaining than Blood Bowl

This review is a difficult one to write. I enjoyed playing it to a point, but it appears that much like a Premium title doesn' translate well to an IAP model, the reverse is also true.
The primary reason I enjoy the game was because I want to see more like it. I enjoy the creative twist on the Snake genre, and this game makes huge strides towards that end. Where it fails was the transition from IAP to Premium game. You find very quickly that the limited leveling system takes AGES. I've probably played this game for over 20 hours (most of my logged time was just having the game on while I did other stuff), and haven't yet finished leveling up all my characters.
This would be fine if the game content were showing me progress as I grind but its not. The same 8 or so levels repeat endlessly, just getting more and more difficult with each run through. So, it's up to you how you define "completing" the game. I'm sick of just playing through the same levels over and over again, and will be stopping my progress now, retiring the title in my library.
If you liked Snake, this title is definitely worthwhile and you can probably get a few hours of enjoyment out of it. But there are other, deeper, titles out there that are probably more worth your gaming dime. If a sequel is coming, I'd wait for that.

The survival aspect was one of, if not the most, important selling point for me and they totally ripped that out of the game. There's no survival feeling at all anymore. And they still haven't come up with any instances for one of the original races! It's three years later and instead of coming up with complete instances for all of the original species, they thought adding a new species was somehow the appropriate action to take.
I think I understand the company. They keep getting a million ideas that they think would be amazing and so they jump all over the place like ADD children on a sugar high. I totally get that—I do, but I really think a bit more organization would benefit this project exponentially. And I think that if they were to take to heart all of the players criticisms, their fan base would stop diminishing.

This is a more straightfoward 4x compared to most 4x games, but i like it because its not overwelmingly complex. I unfortunately missed the original MOO 1-3, but i like the base game enough to get the collectors edition upgrade so i can enjoy the orignals. the only thing im not too impressed about the CE is the Terrans ships are just reskinned red of the human faction ship models.  Tactical combat is fun, but at first it feels way too fast but there are speed options and pause if needed. I really wish there was more than 2 variations of ship models per frigate, destroyer, etc. as there isnt a actual ship builder like GalCiv 3, but mods can fill the lack of variations.
there are some tactical options in combat, such as dodging enemy missiles/fire by hidding behind asteroids, but for the most part fleet engagements are really determined by the quality of your weapos/defenses and a combination of ship numbers or higher quality ships. Starllanes are cool in that they help funnel fleet engaements, which can be very helpful for the AI because there is only a few directions where they can attack you, which in turn forces head on battles and really cuts out the cat and mouse other unrestricted 4x games have.
Empire/colony management is very easy, and so is the pollution and gravity mechanics; you can leave it on autopilot, but you really should manage all pop assignments and production choices to get the most out of it. There are some UI annoyances, like when adding a modification to a weapon, such as making your missiles hardened to resist point defense. The tooltip says the weapon will take 50% more of its base space on your hull, but the weapon card will only show the base vanilla space cost; forcing you to do the calculations your self. Some tech descriptions on the tech tree were cut off on the top of my screen, its little UI stuff like that that can be annoying, but its all minor.
I definety recommend this as a rts and a 4x fan. Especially If you can get it during a sale, keep in mind that unlike alot of other games with dlc factions, this game doesnt allow you to face off againist them as AI unless you own the dlc, same goes for terrans if you dont own the CE.

Such a fun game. I never played it during the glory days (2012-13 I suppose), but still now this can thrill and challenge you.
On an empty server you can play PVE style, scavenging and hunting which is great fun to begin with, but actually it's far too easy. Once you get the hang of it zombies are no threat - you can just run right by them and into a building where they suddenly become slow for no particular reason, then a quick axe to the head and you're off on your way again.
So by all means learn the ropes on an empty server, but get yourself onto a full one asap. The added challenge of other players is what makes this game truly unique and thrilling. You're going to die, a lot, but that's the key point of the game. It takes time to gear up and travel to interesting places, so your character is valuable.
The joy you'll feel at finding a water pump when you're thirsty is balanced perfectly with the fear of getting shot by a bandit as you drink. This game can take you on a real roller coaster ride of emotions and heart-stopping moments. Honestly, the first time you get into a car after 50 hours of endless running is just pure joy.
Others in these reviews seem intent on bad-mouthing the standalone version of this game. I say get both. They're both great.
This version is a simpler one, though its vehicles and the range of weapons is broader. It also has other DayZ-themed mods such as the excellent Epoch (though really that's not DayZ - too easy to get high end gear means less fear of losing it all).
The standalone has far deeper mechanics for survival and player interaction which for me provides a richer and more satisfying experience. All buildings are enterable in the standalone and loot is more spread out, all of which means fewer "hotspots" in each location - and therefore meeting other people is more random and therefore even more heart-stopping! It also has better, more deadly zombies.

I am now going to go against the general opinion of the choir claiming this game is terrible so let the down votes rain! I don't care.
So why the positive opinion, surely i can see the game is a broken heap of promises? literally Hitler etc?
Well no. When it comes to failed Early Access games it really is so that failed EA games on steam can be roughly grouped so that some are big scams made by a egotistical dev that bans everything that moves, Others become leftovers from too ambitious plans.  Darkout is big on the too ambitious plans department. It has lots of potential that partly shows - but will never be fully unlocked.
It is true that this game is 'just another broken down Early Access story' as i can only assume development is stopped and no patches are coming. even for the basic bugs such as elevators.  Surely this state is so bad that this game is now worth zero ...right? Again no. I wasn't there when the promises were made and instead i got this game very cheaply so i can honestly say 'anything goes' as long as it's at least semi entertaining.
So i boldly installed the game and set my aim trying to get atleast some 2-10 hours of gameplay. Since i only paid some euros surely i will get something for that?
Turns out i will get a lot more than that. This game is no Terraria substitute when it comes to gameplay hours so nothing like in the hundreds of hours but tens of hours are pretty much guaranteed and more if you use achievements as a motivator. This game can hold out against Starbound on it's own - at least for awhile before the lack of diversity in biomes and mechanics start to weight in on it (Starbound itself is not a very 'happy camper' either - could be in better shape as it's been in Early Access for a very long time).  Ok so how about Edge of Space?...um. no.that one is a EA chapter on it's own. And then...well there are not that many sidescrolling open world sandbox scifi-survival games that rely on darkness as a element. I am all ears if someone has something like this that blows the competition out of the water and isn't a metroidvania lite-sandbox like Asteria.
So unless you get hit by game not working on Windows10, story data modules not appearing or something else that prevents the game from running properly then you are in for a pretty decent and scary survival treat in the darkness.
Early to mid game is the best this game has to offer. Remember that feeling in Terraria when you went undreground in low wood/copper tier garbage equipment? fearing heights?  That feeling lasted for a very short time. In this game it is constant companion for hours to come and only later will you be able to tackle it partially. Heights just for once is a big problem you will have to deal with and finding the blueprints and ores you need is no small thing. Exploring the colorful but dark caves is hard and dangerous work in this game but down to the mines you must go.
I definitely recommend getting this game on a sale. After installing it leave the prejudices out and also dont look at the (outdated) wikis unless you are completely stuck. Learn the UI and off you go. The best part is the early game: The road from sticks and stones to iron and beyond is a long one and full of peril and i have enjoyed myself so far more than what i expected.

With the progressive style of 10000000, which seems to be noticed very much by many players, this game basically made me be interested to try it out.
Having played the smartphone version before, I knew what I had to expect and went to boot the game.
Basically, you play Snake, just that you don't eat what lies ahead, you kill it. Your snake consists out of heroes which you pick up by killing enemies. You keep unlocking them by beating levels. These heroes can gain levels and have different styles of attacking enemies on the screen. Just like in Snake, you have to avoid walls and in this case enemies to survive, but you also need to guide the rest of the line out of the way! If an enemy touches somebody in the middle of your line, the hero dies and your party gets smaller again. They also can be killed by enemy attacks. The game keeps going as long as you, the leader , remains alive and that can be achieved with the help of power-ups and some buffs you can buy before starting a round.
The currency system, which is gems and tokens, allows you to then boost the duration of power-ups or convert gems into tokens. Gems can also be used to level up a hero faster. Tokens are used for the buffs you buy before staring a round and they also have the use to continue a game when you died. Both of these currencies can be obtained without microtransactions, so don't get fooled by the design of it looking like it would be the case.
In a nutshell I have to say that the price seems fair for this fun game. It offers enough content and also gives you the oppurtunity to play it even when you have only a bit time on the hand. So revive your old-school feelings for Snake and refresh them with this variation of the main-idea!

Quick&Dirty:
Got this game a few days ago at a christmas discount and had good fun with it, making my own little space empires but in the end the AI can't put up a fight, which ultimately gives the game little challenge.
My playthroughs:
I first went into the tutorial and got the game explained to me, but the game was so easy I thought it must be set to a low difficulty setting for the tutorial. I restarted on normal difficulty, but after easily bumrushing my nearest neighbour I restarted on the very hard difficulty and downloaded a balance mod (yay modding!). While the other races put up a bit of a fight in the opening moves of the game, by the mid-game I had a fleet that could crush anything thrown against it, mostly because I had super-large ships, while the enemy was still toying around with flea-sized ships. By then I realised that the game is wonderfully worked out and a good fun space empire sim, but the AI is simply too weak to keep up with an intelligent human player, even if the difficulty setting gives them a resource advantage. This is a pity and ultimately what turns me away from the game, but before I got there I spent a decent amount of hours playing. Looking back, I got value for my money, so this game gets a thumbs up from me.
The good:
Good voiceacting (they really went all-in on the famous actors).
Distinct races.
Lots of empire-building fun.
Active devs (so there's hope for the future!)
The bad:
Poor AI: This is what cripples the game currently for me. The AI can't put up a decent fight, spitting out little ships and measly fleets mid-endgame while my fleet has multiple titans, each of which is capable of wiping out the enemy single-handedly. But it also extends into diplomacy (really bad trades), ship customization and empire expansion. The AI is just not up to the task.
Verdict:
I enjoyed my little space-empire building frenzy. Sure, the AI couldn't put up much of a fight, but I had fun exploring and empire-building and fighting huge space-monsters. I got value for my money (game was discounted) and if you have run out of games to play and nothing new is on the horizon, you can pick up this game to fill the gap. It's not the best, but it's good fun for a while.
Tip:
The Space Amoeba stats are a lie.

Maybe there's a book or something I don't know about, the game sure doesn't explain anything, just leaves you with the feeling of 'I would love to know more about everything'.
That said, did I enjoy the game? Yep.
The combat feels satisfying when you figure it out, even if it's not particularly deep. It's at the level where you might call it brainless action, but every once in a while you need to wake up another brain cell to figure out the right solution, which I at least enjoy once in a while.
I think I bought it discounted to 5€ or maybe less. At that price, I can recommend it, if you're into these kind of games.

I played it, because it was free for a weekend.
I'm big fan of JaggedAlliance/Ufo/XCom/SilentStorm.
Bottom-line:
- it's unbalanced
- constant save/reload needed in missions (savescumming)
- weak story
-----
Pro:
- graphics: the game looks nice
- audio (effects, speaker voices)
- the soundtrack is no bad at all (Squad Loadout)
- customization: modding characters and weapons is lovely - but your new pink sniper rifle named Slayer wont't increase the chance to win a mission ;)
- physics, except grenade throwing
- everything destructable
- shadow / hidden mode is a nice idea
- evacuation on request and on a user-placed location is very nice
Cons:
- the game is unbalanced and buggy
- you can't play a skilled, tactical mission with a good equiped team, randomness will kill you
- the stealth mode doesn't work (carefully positioning your squad in stealth gives you no real advantage compared to rushing in and letting them run into multiple overwatch traps)
- random freezes during missions, several crashes with "GLS Running == 1"
- one needs constant save/reload on hard missions (save scumming)
- you can't skip a lot of cutscenes, e.g. ship landing and leaving
- entering and leaving a mission takes way to long
- you can't skip battle animations (you can't power-rush, because you have to wait)
- i'm not a big fan of timers (they were probably added to break the "set overwatch trap then hide" repeat cycle)
- hud: check how the position of the defense symbol and it's binding change all the time, when switching soldiers (it's a main action, make the position and key static).
- 26 GB download (what makes this game so big?)
- the main story is boring
- autopsy cutscenes are blood-splashingly boring
- clipping issues in maps with high buildings or towers
- what's the scanner for, if i hear the enemy all the time
- why do i need to manage the positioning of scientist and engineers, why not simply auto-assigning them, when they are free

X-Blades is a mediocre hack and slash title which suffers from repetitive gameplay.
You play as Ayumi, a confident treasure hunter who would rather fly solo than share the loot with her teammates. She finds a map leading her to ancient ruins in the hope of finding an artifact of incredible power. The story is very brief is mostly just there to glue the levels together. Immediately apparent is Ayumi's eye-catching appearance (with jiggle physics) in an attempt to sell through sex-appeal and honestly, it's why I played the game in the first place. Just know that it's a budget title beforehand and don't set your expectations too high.
One of the main criticisms I have is with the game's structure over the course of its 40 levels. It can be broken up into 2 parts: the first 20 levels taking place in the daytime and latter 20 being the same levels but only in the evening. The second-half isn't an exact copy of the first but you'll definitely get a sense of déjà-vu as you backtrack through most of the same rooms again only with a darker color change and different monsters to kill.
Using your twin gunswords, Ayumi can slash, shoot and use magic to vanquish foes. This rewards you with 'souls' which is used as currency to purchase new attacks, abilities, spells, damage upgrades etc. You can only have 4 magic abilities active at any one time but they can be swapped around during gameplay. Magic usage is dependent on your rage bar which is filled either by hitting enemies or getting hit yourself.  Strategy is involved as certain enemies can only be defeated by using certain attacks e.g. fire magic against ice enemies or a monster is only weak against guns. You'll know which attacks are effective because the game has a bestiary which sometimes updates before fighting a monster. Sadly the occasions which you have to use specific tactics to kill enemies are quite rare that most of the time the basic attack and starter magic skill 'earthquake' sufficiently clears the level. Large magic skills also plays a short animation before every use, which can get old quickly. Where the combat does shine though is in its boss battles as they require slightly different tactics than the usual normal mobs.
How standard gameplay works is like this: you'll enter a level and a red bar will appear at the bottom right of your screen. You will be locked into that level while waves of enemies spawn around you. Defeating them will reduce the bar and once it's empty, the level is cleared and you're free to explore or progress to the next stage. Rinse and repeat. There are a couple of platforming rooms without combat but these are few and far between. The game will throw hordes of enemies at you and a few stages towards the end were very frantic with seemingly endless amount of enemies. Couple this with the button-mashing gameplay and it can get monotonous.
There are collectables in the game as the end of each level shows a stats screen which details valuables/artifacts and objects destroyed. Often times I found myself clearing a level of monsters and then proceeding to slash and shoot every statue and pot in sight to get 100% level completion. They award souls and rare price discounts on skill upgrades while artifacts power up your attacks.
Also there was strange hit detection when hunting for breakable items, on many occasions my sword attacks did nothing at point blank range until I moved around to find the sweet spot. Hit feedback is another issue as swinging your swords through enemies feels like you're just sliding through them and while being surrounded all the time, it can be difficult to notice you're even getting hit unless you break away from the hypnotizing button-mashing to look at your health bar. The double-jump button timing can be very short and you end up unintentionally performing a single jump, falling short of your goal and sometimes leading to death. It too relies on spamming the button to execute consistently.
The game is very short lasting around 4-5 hours. After completion, there are incentives to start a 2nd playthrough with an unlockable 'Pro' difficulty and bonus costumes which provide additional abilities. There are also multiple endings which are triggered by what skills you've learned by the end of the game.
Graphics-wise, the game exceeded my expectation for a budget title with decent textures and a beautiful, vivid color palette considering the time of original release (Oniblade in 2007). The game looked good in motion with all the combat spell effects and godrays in 60fps. Despite this, the game isn't demanding and runs well on low-end hardware, Windows 10 and is fully compatible with an Xbox 360 controller. No crashes throughout my experience either.
While fighting, an instrumental soundtrack of rocking guitars will play which helps you feel like a badass as you slaughter hundreds of monsters. During some moments, the game will switch to an orchestral score to give that epic battle feeling. Music and sound effects were generally good except that the guns lacked a sense of lethality to them.
Overall, the game has the essence of Devil May Cry but the level design and core gameplay do little to provide a satisfying experience among the monotony of killing rooms of enemies over and over again. The combat is fast and responsive however it devolves into spamming X and the same magic skills.
Usually a cute girl is enough to carry me through a game but unfortunately this wasn't the case in X-Blades.

Where to start here...i'm old enough to have played Kick Off (Super Kick Off on the Master System but also KO2 on WinUAE) as well as Sensible Soccer in various versions and i wonder: Why does this get compared to those games?
I bought this game quite a while ago, the updates are rare and the gameplay just isn't even up to Kick Off 2 levels, let alone Sensible Soccer where you had full control of your team, could set up formations and had to juggle players to avoid the dreaded red X and hoping to get a green mark which. This is not available here, the only thing you have is a basic formation option like 3-3-2, 4-4-2, 4-4-2 diamond, 5-3-2 and the likes but you can't chose your players. There are no substituions either and apparently every team just has 11 players with skills you never see.
The gameplay is very basic on the likes as, as the store page correctly says Microprose Soccer or Tekhan Soccer, nothing fancy, you can't do headers or bicycle kicks. Shooting in high passes to the penalty arey results in some weird shots.
If i had to make a comparison, and i really played a ton of football games (and my faves are still ISS Deluxe, Super Sidekicks 3, Action Soccer, the Nekketsu games on the NES and the few good FIFAs and PESs in between) this really reminds me of World Cup Italia '90 on the Mega Drive/Genesis, though even there players at least could do bicycle kicks and you were able to control the goalie.
The only gamemodes are friendly match, a season (ends after 1, no cups, nothing) and challenge which is some leaderboard stuff, you play against the CPU which gets better game after game until you lose, you get a score, that's it)
The graphics are basic and they don't have the cuteness Sensible Soccer (or some of its clones like Football Glory/Fussball Total from CroTeam) has nor does it look good. You also never see any crowd or the stadium, let alone gags like, again Football Glory had, like the streakers, or a dog chasing the refeere or things like that.
Sound is sparse.
You can change the controls at least but again, the buttons in the menus don't change if you use a gamepad. I changed the controls so shooting is X, Passing is A but while the buttons do their functions, i still get shown B for leaving a menus (which is now mapped on X) which is really amateur.
Honestly, instead of getting this, get Sensible World of Soccer 96/97 on gog for half the price, it's still way more awesome, has a manager mode, tons more teams, tons more playmodes, better gameplay, there's a reason why that game still gets season updates from the community.

This game looks nice, considering it's inspired by the old-school helicopter view classics like sensible soccer. It is also very playable, if you set the game speed to 75 %. This is adjustable from 75 (which feels the most like real life to me) to 125 %, for those who enjoy football at the speed of light (the game lacks any breaking-the-sound-barrier-effects).
As far as the realistic physics go, I can agree as long as the speed setting is set at the aforementioned level. AI is decent, with defenders doing a very good job in getting in the way of your shot. It will take some passing and/or dribbling skills to find space. When playing with a keyboard, this is where the game has serious issues (spoiler alert: all the cons in this review are related to playing this game with a keyboard).
The sprint button is <Esc>! (what the actual...) with the remaining control buttons being the logical A, S, D, and Q, I wonder what grudge the developers have against the W key. There is no way to change these controls. However, it is possible to play without sprinting (just disable it in the settings). This obviously takes the fun of taking on an opponent or even chase a long ball out of the game.
Which brings me to the next issue: there is no way to control the pace and distance of long balls. With short passing, the game will roughly aim the pass at a player that is positioned in the direction your aiming at, making short passing tiki-taka play very managable if you keep an eye on where your opponents are. This aiming feature is not there for long balls: the direction is exactly the one in which the player is running and using the arrows to control the curve of the ball only makes up for so much. Meanwhile this also makes your player move about. As far as power and distance goes, holding the button down seems to work every now and then, but with the ball being released at random moments (and sometimes instantly) when you press the key, this remains guesswork.
This lack of aiming also affects the shooting: while shots will always be powerfull enough to hit the target and holding the button never does anything (this one is actually consistant!), the direction of the shot will again be the same as the direction of running. Playing on a keyboard, this means aiming comes with 45 degree intervals, so there are many positions in and around the box from which it is impossible to get your shot on target. Like with the long passes, controlling the curve of the ball can only make up for so much. All goals I have scored were close range rebounds after the goalkeeper couldn't hold on to the ball.
While there is clearly a lot of effort in this game, it looks good and the physics are very realistic, I cannot recommend this game for those who play with a keyboard. The controls are just too limited and this makes it annoying and boring very quickly.

Bastion is a top-down brawler where you play as one of the few survivors from a calamity that nearly wiped out all life. As 'The Kid', you must battle your way through strange creatures, wildlife, and more in order to keep alive and restore what has been lost.
The gameplay is pretty simple isometric beat-em-up. You have up to two weapons and must make your way through multiple stages while avoiding enemy attacks and falling off the map. Even though the concept is simple, each weapon has a special way to use it for maximum efficency as well as a special move giving just enough depth for the combat to be fun. Each weapon also has a "training ground" which you can visit throughout the game in order to unlock more items and more special moves. The enemies you fight are also varied, making almost each and every engagement exciting as you get to put your skills to the test, never getting too bored of combat. And if you're finding the game too easy, there is an altar with shrines that you find throughout the levels, each shrine increasing the difficulty of the game while rewarding you with extra currency, experience, and so on.
The story isn't so shabby either. The world is represented amazingly throughout the game, each area with it's own unique look and batch of baddies to smash. Through the narrator Rucks and the doodads in the environment you the player learn about the unique history of each area, learning about life before the cataclysm. The plot is slowly revealed to you throughout your journey including who you are, why you're running around at the behest of an old man and what exactly caused the Calamity.
The graphics are good for an indie developer. They were heavily stylized and went well with the game. Each enemy was easily distinguishable and had their own animations which gave you good information on when to block and attack. Each weapon looked unique and had unique attacks. I found no major bugs with them and I found it really convenient when I was launched into the air and some depth was shown as the player character soared through the air. With that said, While the graphics gave character to the game and definitely stood out as really pretty and easy to distinguish objects it only made the game in a minor way compared to the story and gameplay.
The sounds were also really well done. The a few of the songs were really memorable and nothing felt out of place. As well, all the sounds for the enemies were great, including audio cues to go along with the visual cues. The weapons sounded great and had good audio feedback As mentioned above, there were a few memorable songs, but thinking back to the game there wasn't much else that was. Although the music was fine, I'd have to say it was the weakest part of the game.
Overall I'd say the game is a must try, even if you play it on a friends account. It's a really polished, heavily stylized game with lots of unique weapons and enemies, an intruiging story that remains in the shadows for most of the game, and easy to learn hard to master gameplay.

Bought it, and returned it.. Played it again on the free weekend!  I refuse to support 2K games any longer, for reasons Im sure some of you are well aware..
Publisher scumminess aside, I found the game, even on Normal, to be a bit much.. Now ofcourse the "professional" gamers will defend their favorite games to the proverbial death.. One only need venture to a nagative review, complaint thread, or asking for help post to see the immature nature of the great "White Knight", but I digress.. Having played the ever loving hell out of EU/EW, I thought Id be good to go on this one.. Boy was I wrong!  I HATE save scumming, but felt I had no choice here, as majority of the missions have this ridiculous timer.. Sometimes its just to reach an item, leaving you 1 less squadmate in the combat, to sprint to the objective.. Be sure to have 1 action point remaining once arrived, or an entire turn more than said timer states.. Reaching it is not enough! Even if youre standing ON the damn objective, without another turn, or action point, you fail!  Same for evacs!  If you have cleared the board of all enemies, and reinforcements, it does not matter!  You MUST have your squad inside the evac spot, else abandoned!
Theyve added a neat upgrade system, but they are lost upon death, apparently even if you loot your dead teammates drops, you will not reaquire their upgraded weapons, or crafted armor/weapons/utility items!  Very annoying!
The beginning is quite brutal.. Again, the pro players will dispute this to no end.. It seems enemy squads swarm the surrounding areas, often turning one minor engagement, into  your team vs 3 or 4 enemy squads, PLUS reinforcements!Attempting to flank will likely pull unseen squads into the fray.. Insectoid powers can be a nuisance early on, and have twice the health they did previously! Enemy movements, even larger ones seem to be much further than previous! Captains can and will mark, then fire in the same turn (without moving thankfully), and civilians without transform into hulking blob abominations without warning, which can one shot teammates with 5 or 6 health..
Much of this can be forgiven, expected, and/or chalked up to player error.. But the misses both point blank, and on enemies flanked AND out in the wide open, are infuriating, and 'feels' as though it happens too often.. Enemies can and will make the same mistake, and we often forget this when looking back on only the "bad" luck/rng.. But DAMN! 1 bad round can ruin the entire mission, as you really need to push the entire time, toward a timed objective! the misleading hit chance, shooting through walls/cover, and abilities through walls/cover have all returned en masse!  Height likewise, seems less effective than previously..
Theres no real "ramp up" in enemy types.. Within the first handful of missions, youll encounter mechs, Snakes, Abominations blobs, Mutons, etc... Armor, health pools that take an entire round to drain, multiple psionic abilties (sometimes panic work in your favor, but usually not)... Having low health, and weak weapons compounds the issue, and your first game you will likely restart, as youre not really sure what to research first!  Some o fit isnt explained very well, even for a vet of the previous game, as scientists, and engineers work slightly different this time round..
All in all, I find it MUCH less enjoyable than the last.. The timer forces you to often forego tactics and rush objectives you  would never attempt against a dozen enemies with 3/4 squadmates clinging to life.. It does indeed feel like a title more attuned to the masochist, and not at all casual!  Normally, this would play right into my whellhouse, but Im not having fun at all!  When I feel I need to repeatedly save scum, I have had to cheat to win, and thats not me!
This game is truly something else, it is truly one of  a kind, and i am fully aware that some series die off, but i hope the walking dead carries on far past season 3   :)

This isn't really a game but an interactive experience. You can't fail or lose in this. To progress, you simply click on various items in the cabin to invoke memories of the protaganist regarding his relationship with his wife, Serena. As time passes with you clicking on items (even the same items you clicked on earlier) and exploring around the cabin, the protaganist's emotional state undergoes changes (there are three total emotional stages) until the ending approaches.  The total time taken varies from 40-60 minutes.
The point of Serena is not to have fun. The developers were more concerned with leaving an emotional impact on the gamer. In my opinion, they did a solid job at it because the dialogue and progression of emotional stages of the protaganist made the characters feel real and relatable, thus preparing us for the ending twist. To what extent this game has an impact on you, as with any piece of art, depends on what you make out of the experience as well as your own background in intimate personal relationships.
I really feel that this game is a testament to how video games have the capacity to be great art. It's free and short so I recommend that you try Serena. Take your time in the game. Click on items multiple times for the protaganist to say different things and focus on connecting to the character rather than trying to finish it as fast as you can.

Sigh, where to begin....I like Fallout 4, I really do.  I think it's a great game, just not a great Fallout game. Sure, like all of Bethsda's games it has it's share of bugs, but in 600+hours I haven't encountered any game-breaking ones fortunately enough.  Not only do I have 668 hours played as of writing this, I have another 800+ hours on the PS4 version that I purchased day 1 due to not having a good enough PC to run this game.  I have purchased this game and the season pass not once, but twice.
So why the negative review?
Two words:  Creation Club
We didn't want paid mods 2 years ago, and we don't want them now.  And that's not even mentioning their shady pricing of the "Creation Club Credits", or the fact that it's basically ransomware taking up precious space on our drives. I know they've apparently changed this recently to not automatically download all CC content, but I think that's more due to the fact that it's too easy for modders to just create a plugin file for the content without having to purchase it.
Also, they completely lied about CC content being "like miniature DLCs" and "completely original content".  So far, it's all skins, armor and weapons that most have free versions available.  And don't even get me started on the Survival Mode mod for Skyrim SE.  Look, I get that the mod authors want to get paid for their work, I really do.  I am in no way bashing them or their hard work. These mod authors are the reason Bethesda's games have been so great for years now.
This brings me to my next gripe with the CC - the fact that I'm going to have to use 2 more mods now just to counter it's flaws (one to remove it's annoying "Creation Club New" from cluttering my main menu, and another to back up my Fallout4.exe every time they update so that I can continue using my Script Extender).
Anyways, I guess this is the future of gaming - micro transactions, loot boxes and paid mods (that aren't paid mods apparently, but mini DLCs).  I guess I'll be adding Bethesda to my boycott list with the likes of EA and Ubisoft.  The only way for our voices to really be heard is with our wallets.

TL:DR – Third person hack and slash game similar to Darksiders, but very linear. There’s no significant backtracking, and all the puzzles are pretty easy to solve. You can beat the game in less than 10 hours. Technically, it has RPG elements but is extremely simplified.
In Blades of Time you play the treasure hunter Ayumi, a scantily clad, double sword wielding fighter who can kill a whole room full of armed men but can still occasionally act like Lara Croft in the Tomb Raider reboot (whiny and afraid). It’s hard to blame her though because after trying to crash her way into a mythical treasure trove, she and her sidekick Zero (a big buff dude) get thrown into Dragonland. Now separated from Zero, you (as Ayumi) need to find your way through the monster infested Dragonland back to your own world. No, Dragonland doesn’t have any dragons for you to fight, but there are a variety of creeps itching to take a bite out of all your exposed skin.
Gameplay wise, Blades of Time is a third person melee game where you can just mash the attack button and Ayumi will swing her swords like a ninja commando slashing everyone around her. However, unlike games such as Darksiders or Devil May Cry, the enemies aren’t really “stunned” by your hits and can still attack you even as they’re flinching from your strikes. Your attacks don’t interrupt them.  Fortunately you have a short range dash/dodge move that you can use to evade enemy attacks. One thing I noticed is that either the enemies all have a lot of health or your sword strikes are really weak, because killing enemies takes a lot more hits than you would expect.  Seriously, it takes like 20-30 hits to kill anything with your swords. You do have a rifle to shoot baddies with though, and that seems to be pretty strong.
I said before that the game is simplified, and this applies to character development and equipment. You don’t “level up” in the game, and you don’t collect money to buy items with either. As you progress through the story, you “find” new skills or upgrades to your existing ones. They’re unmissable so don’t worry about not finding an awesome spell. All of your equipment upgrades are found using a homing compass that also guides you on which direction you should be traveling. The equipment is missable, but none of it is game changing. They all just boost 1 of your skills, and nothing else (no +armor or +damage). There are only a few magic spells for you to use (fire, ice, and a heavy blast) but they add a little variety to your gameplay. They’re not especially strong either though.
Probably your greatest tool (and the reason for the game’s title) is your ability to reverse time for a short period. During the time reversal, enemies and your past self will re-enact what happened a few seconds ago. During this window you can attack the enemy with your clone for a double or even triple attack (if you reverse time in the middle of another time reversal). This is also used for puzzle solving since there are some areas that you can’t progress without hitting 2 switches at the same time (stand on switch 1 and reverse time, then stand on switch 2 while your clone is still on switch 1).
Pros:
+Simple gameplay and no “research” needed. Don’t worry about character building.
+The game runs smoothly despite having nice graphics for a fantasy world with magic and monsters. My computer didn’t even heat up very much.
Cons:
-If you’re looking for an in-depth RPG like Dragon age, or a loot game like Diablo, Blades of Time isn’t the game for you. Also, the game’s “dialogue” is kind of weird. I don’t know if it’s translated from another language or just badly written at times.
-There is this really annoying bug involving getting your spell casting “stuck” that requires a game restart to fix. It happens a lot in boss battles, and at first I didn’t even realize it was a bug. I thought I had a keyboard button jammed or something. It occurs when an enemy interrupts one of your magic spells.
-The Outbreak multiplayer option plays like a third person MOBA but there’s nobody playing online. Don’t get this game for the multiplayer.
Overall, the game is fun to spend a weekend on, especially if you just want brainless hack and slash without worrying about exploring huge areas or backtracking. You also get to fight large boss monsters and earn some easy Steam achievements. 7/10

There are a few issues though, specifically around the lack of a practice mode, no multiplayer, a lack of details for how to pull off any other moves (if there are any, i.e. banana kick) and most frustratingly, the difficulty spike between easy and normal.
On easy, with natural dribbling on, I win 10, 12 to nothing and can outrun opposition players (the run button seems to work).  Obviously, there isn't much of a challenge at this level.  I change the difficulty to normal and it seems even the mechanics change.  I can no longer run / out-run opponents, they close me down every time and stick to / dispossess without fail.  I can try a passing game, but I encounter the same problem as above, quickly closed down and I don't have (or know of) evasive maneuvres.
This difficulty spike, where elements of the game world seem to have changed to increase the difficulty (i.e. run no longer works and the opposition is faster than all my players), is the biggest problem at the moment.  Sure, I may get through it as I've still won at the normal level, but that the easy mode doesn't really prepare you for the normal mode (run vs. No run) is disappointing and ruins the experience a bit.
I'd still recommend the game, but with the caveats mentioned above.

'Natural Soccer' tends to reminisce in the nostalgic 80's era of sports games, literally the classics such as 'Sensible Soccer' or 'Kick Off'.
I had quite a lot of fun playing this game (even though I'm not a die-hard soccer fan) and it's clear to see that the developer put quite an effort into this game!.
It may look a simple game from up top but beneath the exterior there's much, such as, a bunch of countries to choose from with team's from their respective division's, tweaking of pitch/gameplay conditions, incorporation of difficulty setting's for the goalkeeper's, live replay's, e.t.c.
*Play using a gamepad as it's the only way to truly experience the game and player movement,  using the keyboard is a chore.
Pro's:-
Supports gamepad's.
Lot's of customization setting's for gameplay (replay's, goalkeeper settings,tactic's).
Simple but yet intresting graphics choice (looks like the classic's).
Bunch of countries to choose from, with team's from their division's.
Top-down camera doesn't move sluggish nor too fast (as in some other games).
Polished game with no bugs encountered.
Con's:-
Could add a bit more variation's to the crowd sounds (not that it's bad, just  repititive after a while)
Non-existant tutorial and no keyboard button mapping option. (keyboard doesn't seem to have got much optimization)
Could use a few changes to the score and name display at the bottom. (bit hard to see sometimes)
No player/club customization nor stats or info about them.
The pricing for the game seem's just a tad bit high at $15, would have been great at about $10-$13.
Overall I'd recommend this game since it provides a polished experience with pretty deep gameplay, staying true to the formula which made 'Sensible Soccer' and 'Kick Off' great.

Oldschool top down football (soccer) game inspired by the old classics from the 90s. If you liked those games (KO2/Sensible Soccer) you will like this game. Nothing has quite captured the essence of those games until now. Scoring a goal in in the current generation of 3D football computer games (FIFA/PES) never quite give you that feeling that you earned it. In Natural Soccer, as in the classics from the 90s, it can finally feel like you earned scoring that goal again.
But a note of warning to all those that think that winning in games should be served up to them on a silver platter: it is not an easy game. You will battle the control of the ball as much as you battle the opposing team but in my humble opinion this is what really should be like. There are easier control options provided for those that really prefer this, but you will still have to earn that win all by yourself. And when you do win, you will want to feel that way again.
All in all a Natural Soccer is a good football (soccer) game for those that like a bit of a challenge.

Master of Orion is both a massive hit and miss depending on your perspective. The game has clearly been lovingly crafted to be faithful to the original trilogy games but where it falls off is in the level of simplicity that has been incorporated into the game. This isn't necessarily a bad thing though.
So what is the bad? Well when your game is sequel to another you usually expect some kind of innovation to the game's mechanics to make it new and exciting, not just a reskin. Master of Orion is at it's bare bones a reskin of Master of Orion 2 and doesn't seem to try anything new mechanically. The good though is that this game has clearly been a labour of love, from the effort put into getting iconic sci-fi voice voice actors to the universe itself constantly and enthusiastically encouraging you to expand and explore this game is very much, a good game. Unfortunately though it may fall short of your expectations of a 4x grand strategy or of a sequel.
With all that said though Master of Orion is truly made for new players and makes for a great introductory point to 4x strategy. The user interface is easy to understand, doesn't clog up the display and is very elegant, the galaxy and worlds look amazing, colourful and alive, and there is exceptional voice acting to help make even the most mundane tasks enjoyable.
This game is worth trying out, if you find it's too simple you can easily just ask for a Steam refund but if you do end up liking it you will find yourself engrossed in this game for hours at a time.
