Blood Bowl: Chaos Edition is a faithful reproduction of the board game. You have all the rules and teams and a big community that enjoys the game.
While it did take Cyanide quite some time to fix all the bugs, it is now running pretty well and stable for years.
The game itself centers around getting the ball into the enemies endzone to score a touchdown. How you do this is up to you and the different fantasy-races usually employ different methods of doing so. The woodelves dance around their enemies with grace, while teams like chaos prefer to beat their opponents into a pulp first and then worry about the ball.
Rulewise it is a game about risk-management. Many actions carry a risk of failure and if something goes wrong your turn ends. So you must plan your turn in advance and start with actions that carry no or a low risk, But a bad roll of the die can still screw your plans which is just part of playing Blood Bowl. A good "trainer" knows that those failures will happen and patiently waits for his fortune to reverse. Still, it's a very tactical game overall and it is very satisfying to see your plans work like clockwork !
No game is perfect however, so there are some cons:
- To really understand the game you should try to find the rulebook online. The provided manual does not provide much help. Doesn't apply if your already a fan of the board-game, but will be a hurdle for new players.
- The UI could be better and you could get better information about the chance of success for your actions. Again mostly a problem for people who don't know the rules well.
- The options to modify your teams appearence are very limited. You can pick a color a symbol and choose between a very limited set of skins/models for your players. In the actual game however it makes little to no difference so it's not a big deal.
- The AI may seem strong at first but you quikly learn how to beat it no matter the odds and the difficulty settings. It's good enough to train against but the real fun is playing against other people. The singleplayer can still be enjoyed for a long while... constantly winning has an appeal of it's own ;)
- While the AI-commentators do have a quite an array of comments it doesn't take that long until it gets boring. Thankfully you can turn them off once you've reached that point. Same goes for the touchdown animations, but hey, you only see these if someone scores a touchdown which isn't that often anyways... and as long as you made that point you wont care.
Now don't let these cons get in your way of having a good time with this game. It's really worth it in my opinion, it just wouldn't be fair to not mention them.
So, what are you waiting for ? Get a team together and have a go at the trophy.
It's a show of skill, of might, it's entertaining... it is BLOOD BOWL !

After buying so many failed EA titles in the past, I was very hesitant to pick this one up. Eventually, I dove in and bought it to see what it's like for myself. At the time of writing this review, I have no regrets.
I must say that graphic-wise, this game is not that bad. When you're in the crows nest of your ship looking over the horizon, the ocean/lightning looks amazing. Also, hitting an enemy with a cannonball and watching them fly 40 ft through the air also adds to the entertainment, so 10/10 for ragdoll physics.
Performance-wise, the game is also good. I would have called it "great" if it weren't for the (subtle) drops in fps. With an MSI GTX 1070 and a i7 6700k @ 4.6ghz, I usually run between 110 - 150 fps on ultra, but those numbers fluctuate quite a bit. I have also yet to experience any significant "gamebreaking" glitches although I have heard reports of players getting stuck on cannons, stuck in loading screens, menu buttons not clickable, etc. But these are expected from an EA title & most likely will be fixed in the near future. 7/10
Gameplay-wise, the game is FANTASTIC. It actually makes you feel like you're apart of the ship's crew. It's very exciting when you engage in an enemy ship, because you can choose to fire your cannons and slowly sink her, grapple and board, or even ram the side for that matter. From what I've seen, slowing the enemy down/injuring their boat followed by a grapple is the most effective method. When you grapple an enemy, it becomes a "1 life elimination game", causing the respawn time to increase to 100+ seconds. Your objective at this point is to kill all their crew before they kill yours, and you win. 10/10
Extra Notes: One more thing I'd like to add is the voice acting done for the "z" "x" commands. When you say "CHARRRRRRRRRGEEE" as the english, you sound literally like Nigel Thornberry and it's god damn hilarious. Not to mention when you have teammates actively using their microphones to simulate pirates.

I hate to write a bad review for an indie game shop, especially one that produced the brilliant Machinarium.  I also know I'm going against a tide of positive reviews from both users and pro reviewers I respect greatly.  Apparently, I have no heart or soul.
But seriously...what the hell?  This is not a game.  It's a trippy surreal click through random psychodelic cutscenes  with no apparent goal or purpose.  Yes, I know there is (sort of) a bad guy and a goal, but that doesn't really have much to do with any given scene.  Lots of people describe the art as "beautiful" or "charming" but it's all just minimlist soft-focus psychodelia.  Maybe if you were REALLY stoned it would be awesome, but otherwise it's just odd.
And I'm somebody who really appreciates weird and surreal indie games.
The main problems:
1) There's no emotional connection to the characters or environment, like in Machinarium.  If you CARE about what you're clicking on, games like this can be a lot of fun.  But I can't even tell WHAT I'm clicking on most of the time.  (Unless it's just another goddamn leaf or berry.)
2) It's all random "click-on-everything-and-see-what-happens".  If there's no intentionality, there's no puzzle solving, and no game.  Just a lot of clicking on random stuff to get random effects (that sometimes move the "story" forward).
So...no.  Just...no.  I loved Machinarium and I hope they make a sequel, but this game is the polar opposite, and I cannot recommend it.

The game where you can play Farming Simulator 2009, but really unpolished and feeling more incomplete then a half-eaten apple. I can see the developers had great ambition however it was clearly wasted on details and other components that are not needed directly for the foundation of a farming simulator.
In real farm you are an aspiring farmer growing from helping hand to true independent farmer where you don’t have to rent everything you find, the only problem is that this is not a Bethesda RPG it’s a farming simulator; the game suffers from many problems, although most of the core aspects are there many nice yet unimportant things have been added at cost of the base game. On the steam page you can see the vision the developers have for the game, and when you play it you can see all the things they have not achieved.
Out of all the parts of the game this one is done the best, it has impressive visuals which look good and are pleasing to the eye. Sadly the developers have forgotten that a game should not rely on its graphics to be good. Instead it should rely on its gameplay and other aspects; as I saw the realistic shadows flow through a cornfield I thought:
.
Not only graphics but physics as well, when the objects actually collide when they’re supposed to, are quite enhanced as well as parts of my supersized lawnmower could get dislodged after I rammed it into the only car on the highway in the surrounding 200 miles.
This also goes for the UI (User Interface) which besides from looking exactly like Farm Simulator does function like it’s supposed to, weirdly enough some of the options are incredibly useless or are another case of “wasted resources”.
Real farm seems very incomplete. often I can find myself wanting to do things that I can’t, doing things that should be implemented and doing things that should not be possible by the laws of gravity. I feel like the developer has gone from the basics of the game to the most tiny details and worked on from there, there is a large economy system with multiple farms everywhere and deposits yet no one is around; the place is a ghost town with 1 car driving around which sadly cannot be destroyed by a combine harvester.
I can go up to another farmer’s land, farm his crops and go back again to sell them at the local deposit, not only is this an indication that the game isn’t finished it’s also an indication that in the world of Farming thievery is apparently a much more profitable career then farming your own crops.
The supposed tutorial In the game is practically a large list of tasks you have to complete because of the game wanting you to do so. In this “tutorial” you have to complete a list of boring tasks which mostly include do this for 100% or do that to… Not only does this not count as a tutorial it’s also lazy level design because to me it looks like the developers really didn’t care about the player understanding what he was doing.
Overall the sounds are alright though when driving for long periods, which you are going to be, they can become a bit annoying. The soundtrack however is definitely not so, it opens nice and charming and eventually keeps repeating itself until you go into the nicely crafted settings menu to turn it off. Sadly the soundtrack has also become a victim of “We put too much money in the graphics”
Real farm is just not finished, I can see that it still has potential but right now it just cannot compete with any of the other games in this genre because of its limitations. If the developers keep working on this and patching the massive holes in its core foundation then perhaps it can one day truly shine above the rest but now is not that time.
And developers, please let me drive into a river with my 350.000 dollar tractor.

Sim games are hard to make. Simulating real world physics and biological systems require expertise AND experience. For each subject.
Add to the complication that this game is entering a sub-genre with 2 already established titles battling for suppremacy. That gives us a little perspective on what we can expect from a new entry.
Real Farm IS NOT yet a good game. It DOES have what it takes to be a good game, provided that we can do the work to help them get there. The price is too high right now and the game is closer to early access than Gold release. That's not a complaint against the developer, but rather the publisher who has to keep budgets and release dates balanced.
The good news is that the developers are using the sales to fund a rapid support schedule. The beta branch of the game is really cranking out the fixes and improvements. I'm quite optimistic that they will have a real new series contender here. If we are bold and brave as consumers. Nobody will ever make better games in this genre unless we buy the games. The genre needs to be making enough money for developers/publishers to want a piece of it. So buy the games, push developers to improve them and reap the rewards. If you want the farm game of the future, do the work now.
What the game does right: It's a lot like Farm Sim 16 if we are being honest. It has good music, decent art assets, the menus work well enough, etc.
What it does wrong currently: physics(wacky flipping/flying tractors over the mountains are possible), sound(hooking up tools is silent, no working sounds for many jobs, etc), no licensing(future games likely to have, provided people buy this), weather effects.
There is a good game here. If you want to push this game or other farm games to improve faster, there needs to be competition. That means you have to buy them all. Your move farm/sim gamers.

I first picked this up back in October 2014, played it for a good few hours, then put it aside. Started playing it again a couple of weeks ago and found that development seems to have ceased some time ago.
The game isn`t fully finished (and likely never will be) and the devs have disappeared, "So why are you recommending it?" I hear you say.
Well, that`s because what is present in the game is actually quite good. I`ve played various 2D side scrolling crafters, and Darkout is a definite step up, it`s a real shame it won`t be 'finished'.
For one thing, it looks really nice, I mean really. The textures are smooth, the backgrounds are actually worth studying, never mind the foreground. The art team have made an effort and it shows (especially in the stratosphere).
The whole concept of the plants and creatures adapting to the darkness makes for an interesting change to the usual environment. Just moving through the jungle biome with all the glowing plants and the fireflies drifting around is surprisingly enjoyable. As is taking the jetpack above the clouds and exploring the skylands.
I`ve yet to craft the underwater propulsion doodad, so I don`t know what (if anything) is to be found in the depths of the ocean.
The crafting. There is a lot of stuff to play with. Build power generators and lay wiring networks to connect up lights, teleporters, elevators, gun turrets, and your crafting stations. One definite thing I love is that you don`t need materials in your inventory. Heave everything into chests/closets/storage vaults and as long as the container is nearby then the game knows what`s there, and draws whatever you need from wherever it is.
I haven`t reached the end of the tech levels so I haven`t yet came across any gamebreaking bugs that others have encountered. In saying that, the elevators are a little...quirky, I suspect mostly due to their speed.
One of the biggest issues seems to be finding the datacubes, but I found all I needed pretty quickly (so far anyway). Once I went to the relevant biome the mobs were dropping the cubes like confetti at a wedding.
Yes, it can be a little grindy and repetitive (if you`re intent on quick completion), but I think I`ve found that with most games like this, and I do find it amusing to see people complaining about the story. After all, I don`t recall Minecraft having a riveting plot...
I`m not really focussing on reaching the endgame as soon as possible. My goals at the moment are:
- build storage tanks for all the tar I come across (there`s a feature/bug involving liquids and buckets which means tar and water are unlimted, but underground tar pools are still a nuisance)
- dismantle the city for all that lovely titanium
- find those damn crystal caverns
- use my newly crafted GPS to find sea level, then drill a tunnel from my base to the shore (why move to the beach when you can bring the beach to you? ;) ) so I can use the limitless waters of the ocean to drown the underworld.... Muah hah hah hah

First off the good: The graphics for the most part are great, in my opinion. The music, too. The voice acting for the player character is well done, and Serena's is not bad either. Also, while I don't really like the writing or handling of it, the premise of the game has potential, and the first part of the game is actually pretty good.
Now, onto the bad: The writing is what kills the game. The pacing is too slow in the beginning, and too fast in the end (which leaves the characters with very little depth), and the "twist" you find at the end is something you'll guess as soon as you start exploring. The atmosphere is ruined by things like the silly book titles and the narrator's dialougue going from a melodramatic plea to remember to him casually speaking when you run through dialougue options. And then the ending. I don't want to spoil anything for anyone who's considering playing the game, so let's just say that the graphics and voice acting take a considerable drop in quality, any themes or atmosphere created in the last thirty minutes are ruined, and the last shot is a cliche that will leave you groaning.
I really hate to be so critical to a game that was free, but I was really surprised by it after I read so many positive reviews. Overall, I'd say it's a game that will cost you nothing but your time to play it, so if you're really desperate to kill an hour (or you don't mind a bad story if there's good graphics or sounds), go ahead, but otherwise, I'd just find something else.

The single-player-only game features a career mode with a simple tutorial and a free play mode where you start out with basic equipment. The interface is terrible across the board: the camera is erratic, the mouse sensitivity cannot be adjusted, the keyboard controls cannot be changed and there is not a list of even what they are (only gamepad controls are listed in the options screen), the map is too small, and it can be difficult to get into equipment. While the equipment have good models, the graphics feature poor road textures at a distance and graphical glitches like glowing lines spanning across fields. The game world is small, with only occasional cars and nobody else working the fields (including workers you can hire). Gameplay consists of driving across the same fields over and over again using different attachments to plow, cultivate, sow, fertilize, water, and harvest crops. You can raise animals, but this offers only a small amount of variety. You can also take jobs at other farms, but they are the same jobs available otherwise. Vehicle handling is poor: every vehicle accelerates and brakes at the same rate, and getting stuck on small objects is too easy. Real Farm doesn’t offer anything new or different, and what it does offer is significantly worse than the competition.

This game is overlooked.
Imagine Shadow Of Mordor but without an open world element. Now imagine an interesting story line with some voice acting that does its best to make fun of the main characters hair color. The game play definitely nails it on this one.
You start off as an adventurer going to Dragon Land in search of treasure. Obviously things aren't as they seem and you run into foes of all sorts. One's that stalk in the shadows to big bosses that will have you dashing, sort of flying, and dodging every which way. The game does a good job mixing up enemies and tries not to bombard the player with boring old schemes. The game is sort of like Too Human where you fight multiple enemies and can attack them with varying sequences. X is the button to attack with your swords while pushing in the right thumb stick will equip your gun (which can be modified or changed as the game progresses given you are picking up the treasures along the way).
This is where it get's interesting though : along the way altars are available that give you certain abilities that you are able to choose from (such as using fire, ice, or a slide attack technique). For instance, if there is a lot of enemies you can press B then X to unleash a fire attack. To do these special attacks however your character needs enough "rage" to be built. This is done by attacking enemies. With rage other special attacks are available or you may choose to heal yourself. The diversity in the attacks hasn't put me to boredom yet. Right button when a player is injured enough will put the player into an animation (some sort of decapitation involving the foe). This is the best part though and why the game is called Blades of Time... within the game by pressing left button the player is able to rewind time and rewind themselves and their foes. Yes, you rewind your player but your player is immobile and doesn't move as time is rewound. This means that even though you attacked one foe already, you can rewind time, then play it forward again and have two of your characters (of one you control) attack the enemy. This process can be repeated sort of by will after it's learned. Heck if you want you can keep rewinding and have one of your characters attack him with blades, one with a gun, one with specials etc... it is possible. The game's difficulty is also at an appropriate level.

For years I have been looking for a simple soccer game to replace my SWOS and Total Soccer addictions, and although Addictive Soccer, Throw In and Yoda Soccer have been decent attempts they weren't quite what I was looking for.  However, last year I came across this beauty and although it had humble beginnings (the generic blue team vs the generic red team) I felt this could go far.  And it has...
It's a great little game which you can pick up and play for a few minutes for a quick fix, or take on a league if you have a spare couple of hours.  The gameplay is the old cliché - easy to pick up and difficult to master - and it can also be very challenging, often leaving me wondering how the AI cut through my defence with such precision.
It's refreshing to see a developer being so responsive to their customer’s comments - in its short life he has added two new control mechanisms, changed a multitude of settings and the game just gets better and better with each release.  This little game has big plans, and I can't wait to see how far it goes!
An editor is the next big step to allow players to create their own teams, and the potential that we could have another playable, career based soccer game is something I am really looking forward to.  If you like Sensible Soccer, Kick-Off or Total Soccer then do yourself a favour and pick up this gem.  If you like PES or FIFA, do yourself a favour and play a game where quick thinking and your actions with the controller actually make a difference!

With the newest update, 1.4.0, i finally feel comfortable giving this game a solid positive review.  Before the update, i was not on the fence as to weather it was a good game or not.  It still is and was a good game, with amazing support from the developer, who actually gives a damn about his product and the people who purchase it.
However, the game felt a little lacking.  I felt less control than i would have liked.  I dont mind hard games and challenges, but i also dont want to feel cheated by the limitations of the simplicity of the game.
That is where the beauty is in this one.  You can tweak the settings to suit your gameplay style. The developer gives you the option to make this game your own.  With each update, he doesnt remove options for the player, he just adds more and more.
speaking of this most recent update, that is what got me to write the review.  I saw the update note and thought it was going to be the much anticipated player editor. While that will be an amazing addition when it eventually comes, this update was a welcome surprise for me.  Adding the sprint option to speed up gameplay and really let me use the open pitch and give me the ability to get around defenders was wonderful.  Then also adding the "easy" dribbling control to go along with it, so that it was really my doing when i lost the ball to the defense by being sloppy with turbo or passing was the icing on the cake.  I feel like i lose or win now based on my actions on the pitch.  The first touch is noticeable, i dont feel as though the defense is stripping me of the ball nearly as often as before, because i can turn and run.
Notes:

-This is a hard game, easy to pick up and play (especially with friends) but difficult to master
-This game almost requires a controller to play, but the controls are tight and responsive
-There are still some improvements to be made, but the arrow is always pointing up as this is clearly a passion project that deserves the support of anyone who is interested.
If you are a fan of the classic soccer/futbol games of years past, this is a title you must pick up. With a developer that gives great support and is always updating and improving the game based on suggestions from players like you and I, This game feels fresh and like its improving on a successful formula. I can now proclaim it is a great game.

Quite simply "Natural Soccer" is how football games used to be in the 80's so if you ever played the classics such as Kick Off or Sensible Soccer then you will feel perfectly at home playing this great little football game. Before Kick Off arrived football games were pretty much the same with the ball being quite literally stuck to the player's foot but Kick Off changed the rules and we had total freedom and control of the ball as we do today in Fifa and Pes.
Well Natural Soccer may just as well be called Kick Off as it's virtually the same, graphics are as simple and fluid as they always were but they sure do move nice and fast and really smooth as well and OpenGL really does do it justice, controls are very easy to pick up if you have played this type of game before but could take some getting used to if you haven't but it is designed to have total ball control which it does with ease so practice will be required. Soundwise there really isn't much to say as it just the crowd with a few whistles and kicks so it would be nice to have a bit more in there but it still sounds great for what is there.
In the game there is a league which works well but would like the addition of say a cup competion or indeed a tournament and just imagine online multiplayer but seeing as they are not in there and just the league this still makes for a good challenge but at least you can change the difficulty if you so desire once you start getting some good results, one good option would be to have a practice mode this i'm sure would benefit a lot of gamers wanting to hone their skills especially for ball control as well as free kicks, corners and penalties and i would love to see referees ingame as well but these are just minor things and doesn't detract from an otherwise awesome game but please do play it with a gamepad or joystick or you will just be at a disadvantage.
For me personally i have to say this brings so many memories back and one good thing i found is that having owned the game previously before it came to steam is that my saves were still intact and recognised that right away so i didn't have to start over, just to sum up that if you played those old 80's classics you will feel right at home playing Natural Soccer but if you have only been used to Fifa or Pes then you might not find it to your liking and may find it a little frustrating or difficult but it's there to be mastered so why not give it a go?

After buying so many failed EA titles in the past, I was very hesitant to pick this one up. Eventually, I dove in and bought it to see what it's like for myself. At the time of writing this review, I have no regrets.
I must say that graphic-wise, this game is not that bad. When you're in the crows nest of your ship looking over the horizon, the ocean/lightning looks amazing. Also, hitting an enemy with a cannonball and watching them fly 40 ft through the air also adds to the entertainment, so 10/10 for ragdoll physics.
Performance-wise, the game is also good. I would have called it "great" if it weren't for the (subtle) drops in fps. With an MSI GTX 1070 and a i7 6700k @ 4.6ghz, I usually run between 110 - 150 fps on ultra, but those numbers fluctuate quite a bit. I have also yet to experience any significant "gamebreaking" glitches although I have heard reports of players getting stuck on cannons, stuck in loading screens, menu buttons not clickable, etc. But these are expected from an EA title & most likely will be fixed in the near future. 7/10
Gameplay-wise, the game is FANTASTIC. It actually makes you feel like you're apart of the ship's crew. It's very exciting when you engage in an enemy ship, because you can choose to fire your cannons and slowly sink her, grapple and board, or even ram the side for that matter. From what I've seen, slowing the enemy down/injuring their boat followed by a grapple is the most effective method. When you grapple an enemy, it becomes a "1 life elimination game", causing the respawn time to increase to 100+ seconds. Your objective at this point is to kill all their crew before they kill yours, and you win. 10/10
Extra Notes: One more thing I'd like to add is the voice acting done for the "z" "x" commands. When you say "CHARRRRRRRRRGEEE" as the english, you sound literally like Nigel Thornberry and it's god damn hilarious. Not to mention when you have teammates actively using their microphones to simulate pirates.

Man, I really wanted to like this game.  I played through and beat the last X-Com game with little fanfare, sure it had it's moments but Jesus is this a step up in difficulty.  One of the things I found really frustrating is that the early game enemies start with mind control and got to experience it first had on the first mission of the game. So right out the gate I lose one of the four members of my team with no recourse. I understand this game is supposed to be hard but punish me for things I do wrong, not just randomness.
This would be fine if it wasn't for the larger issue at hand, the timers. I'm all for being the scrappy underdog and losing guys along the way, hell, the playthrough in the first game I lost loads of guys on missions.  The timers in this game are in basically every mission which seems incredibly counterintuitive when you are supposed to be stealthy and cautious.  So what am I supposed to do, rush the objective or set up an ambush, I cannot do both.
I am sure there are plenty out there who will lambast me for not being good enough, but again, I played and beat the first game, nothing here is new but I got my♥♥♥♥♥♥♥kicked.  I'm fine with this, I love Dark Souls after all but this game honestly feels really cheap.  If it isn't mind control, it's enemies who see me across the map or snakes pulling my guys across the map.  Naturally these are all abilities given no explanation as why would they announce them, but the issue here as I mentioned earlier is that these abilities are incredibly lethal.  So on top of trying to be as stealthy as possible due to a timer, early cheap enemy abilities, and cutscenes constantly freezing my game so people can tell me things I already know I find it to be a very grating experience. I tried, I really tried.
Now it's not all bad, the whole sword thing is great, as are some of the upgrades (swords that stun? yes please), but the game is stressful and exhausting.  The difficulty feels cheap, the pace is exhausting (timers and people constantly yelling at you) and you don't really have time to actually ENJOY the game.
There are some cool ideas but timers do not mix with stealth, they just don't.  Have all the doom clocks you want but not everything needs to autodestruct.  At least not right away, you could easily have made many of those timers dark events.  Make them something the player would want to spend time/resources to counteract.  As I said earlier, I really want to like this game but it's entirely too stressful for the payoff.

The Walking Dead is bassed of a comic of Robert Kirkman's. The game tells the story of Lee (a convicted criminal) and Clementine (a young girl in the Apocalypse). Basing the story off of the two characters alone would not give the game justice. Unlike most games, Clementine isn't as annoying as you might think. Infact she is really humorous and you begin to have a connection with her as you progress.
You meet other survivors such as, Glenn (for a short time) Lily, her father Larry, Kenny and his family, Doug, Carley, and a ton of other characters along the way. The character interaction is probably the best part about the game, as what you say will determine whether or not someone trusts you, or even likes you. It's not just about speech, as actions also determine whether or not if they like you or hate you.
It's incredibly difficult to go on to explain why this game is so great without going into spoiler territory.
The game is well worth the $25 dollars alone, but at the moment it's on sale for $6.30. TAKE THE DEAL. You will not be dissapointed!

This turned out to be a pretty fun action game, though it took a while to get going and I didn't like it as much as, say, Marlow Briggs.
Ayumi has, unfortunately, only one basic melee attack that you just keep spamming to work up your "rage meter", which then lets you fire off spells. There's also a Dash move for dodging and closing the distance, and you can switch to a ranged weapon which significantly slows you down and makes you unable to Dash. Once an enemy is at low health, you have the option to perform a finishing move - or just keep wailing on them until they go down. There is also "kick" to break blocks that you rarely need to use. All in all, it's pretty uninspiring until you get enough spells to spice up the combat, and really start using the Rewind Time ability.
Rewind Time is actually pretty interesting - it rewinds the world around you, while leaving your character alone. Your character's position and any damage you've taken still stays, so you can't "undo" fatal mistakes like you could in the Prince of Persia games.  Rewinding Time creates a "time clone" of you, that then proceeds to go through all the actions you've taken during those "rewound" seconds. So you could unload half a rifle clip at a charging enemy, rewind time as they get close, and then continue shooting. Their health will be back to where it was at the beginning, but they'll start taking double damage because there will now be two of you shooting! This is actually required for some enemies who are surrounded by magical force fields that can only be broken by extremely concentrated hails of bullets.  Rewind Time is also used for some basic puzzles, such as when multiple pressure plates/switches must be triggered at the same time
Most bosses require some strategy to defeat, but it's usually not hard to figure out, and serves as a nice change of pace.
You start with the double-jump, which is always appreciated.  As you proceed in the plot, you unlock new spells & abilities, find new equipment (a magical compass pointing the direction of any nearby equipment chest is very useful), and demolish boatloads of enemies.
TL;DR - Fun game once you get enough spells/abilities to make the combat less boring, just don't expect something on the level of Devil May Cry, God of War, or even Marlow Briggs.

Though it has flaws, Blades of Time is no doubt potentially a fun game.  I say "potentially" because if it weren't for the massive framerate drop during the entire game, the repetiive enemies, the uninteresting characters, predictable gameplay, terrible platforming, and the puzzles, I would say this would be a buy instead of a rent.  Despite being "Limited Edition" version, all that is "limited" is an extra level which you play as a different character...which should've been an option from the start.  (Why is it that "Limited Editions" are the "complete package" again?)  The idea of having your avatar go back in time to use your past selves to fight alongside your present version is a great gameplay mechanic, especially when used in the right way such as fighting enemies.  The main problem is, like any other hack-and-slash game, this mechanic is often pushed to the side or being thought of as a secondary option for combat rather than being the focus.  The enemies are repetitive, making the gameplay predictable as you will be forced into implementing the same strategy to defeat the same enemy over and over again, which doesn't add much to the "time" mechanic when you think about it.  The game tries to give you a break from combat to do some puzzles, but they are not very exciting and are WAY too easy to complete (I hate puzzles anyway).  The only challenging level was the desert level where if you touch the hot sand, you will die, forcing you to use the shade as a literal cover.  No other game I know of has a creative level like that!  Also, the characters are so bland, and the main charcter Ayumi NEVER SHUTS UP!  Always with the complaining!  Other M syndrome, anyone?  Finally, the controls are VERY clunky.  The jumping mechanic is especially annoying and tedious because when you jump, you either automatically "bounce" or slide before you come to a complete halt, and it makes the platforming sections all the more frustrating.  This is something MANY modern platforming games whether 2D or 3D shouldn't be doing.  In the end, Blades of Time has the potential to be something more, but in the meantime, I suggest renting this game instead of buying it.

Man, I really wanted to like this game.  I played through and beat the last X-Com game with little fanfare, sure it had it's moments but Jesus is this a step up in difficulty.  One of the things I found really frustrating is that the early game enemies start with mind control and got to experience it first had on the first mission of the game. So right out the gate I lose one of the four members of my team with no recourse. I understand this game is supposed to be hard but punish me for things I do wrong, not just randomness.
This would be fine if it wasn't for the larger issue at hand, the timers. I'm all for being the scrappy underdog and losing guys along the way, hell, the playthrough in the first game I lost loads of guys on missions.  The timers in this game are in basically every mission which seems incredibly counterintuitive when you are supposed to be stealthy and cautious.  So what am I supposed to do, rush the objective or set up an ambush, I cannot do both.
I am sure there are plenty out there who will lambast me for not being good enough, but again, I played and beat the first game, nothing here is new but I got my♥♥♥♥♥♥♥kicked.  I'm fine with this, I love Dark Souls after all but this game honestly feels really cheap.  If it isn't mind control, it's enemies who see me across the map or snakes pulling my guys across the map.  Naturally these are all abilities given no explanation as why would they announce them, but the issue here as I mentioned earlier is that these abilities are incredibly lethal.  So on top of trying to be as stealthy as possible due to a timer, early cheap enemy abilities, and cutscenes constantly freezing my game so people can tell me things I already know I find it to be a very grating experience. I tried, I really tried.
Now it's not all bad, the whole sword thing is great, as are some of the upgrades (swords that stun? yes please), but the game is stressful and exhausting.  The difficulty feels cheap, the pace is exhausting (timers and people constantly yelling at you) and you don't really have time to actually ENJOY the game.
There are some cool ideas but timers do not mix with stealth, they just don't.  Have all the doom clocks you want but not everything needs to autodestruct.  At least not right away, you could easily have made many of those timers dark events.  Make them something the player would want to spend time/resources to counteract.  As I said earlier, I really want to like this game but it's entirely too stressful for the payoff.

As a turn-based strategy game, XCOM2 has done well in overall. Its imbalance in enemies and time-limit design make the game more challenging, forcing players to plan the movement more carefully and sometimes more risky. In personnel, I quite enjoy this kind of challenge, if there is no RNG factor.
In comparison to XCOM:EU, XCOM2 requires a better resource planning in the beginning. Or, you will pay your debt during progression because your enemies will always outperform you in "hardware". To work around, you need stronger weapons to set up a plan, eliminating a group of enemies within one turn.
The only one thing frustrates me is RNGesus in this game. You want to hack for battle advantages? RNG. You want to hit your enemies? RNG. You want to finish your scanning before raids? RNG. You want to win a battle certainly? 100% chance to hit your every enemies or pray RNGesus. This issue also exists in XCOM:EU, but it's not very annoying since you can resolve with sufficient preparation before hands. In XCOM2, imbalance in forces and time-limit will teach you lessons, unless you install mods to mitigate them.

I was going to make a full review of this game. Recommending it. Till I found out that there is no tactical combat, and only auto-resolve for battles in multiplayer. Until that changes I can't possibly recommend this game. If you want to play a MOO with autoresolve, just play FreeOrion, which is, yes, a free game. You'll be better off than playing this game in the current state. Or simply play one of the classics.
Again, there is plenty of good things in this MOO, and it's ok to play a few times in single. But with a multi without tactical combat, or at least the ability to watch the battles in spectator way. The game just isn't worth the price tag. It's a good start. A base of a game to start from and add to it, perhaps in an expansion. BUT, the fact that there is autoresolve only in multiplayer makes it targeting a much narrower group of players who have many other titles to choose from if they wanted an autoresolve driven experience.
So I have to sadly add MOO to the list of failed space 4X games that didn't live up to their full potential. If you want an actual 4X in space done right. Check out:
Sword of the Stars
Endless Space
MOO 3 (Strawberry/Vanilla/Tropical modded), MOO 2
(Galciv 3 could be a great choice too, but since I haven’t played it yet I can’t really recommend it)
Otherwise today's 4X games, keep being released either with no multiplayer at all, or with this kind of crippling decisions to make it autoresolve only. This niche of players, who want to enjoy what was a standard 20 years ago - space 4X games with multiplayer and tactical combat. Before this “less is more” ideology came about and ruined franchises like Command and Conquer. Must just bite the bullet, and realize that today making games like Sims is more profitable than actually making good space 4X games. Or so it seems. This is not just the problem of this MOO. It's the problem of whole industry as you can list all good space 4X games on the fingers of both hands if not just one hand on Steam. Sadly.

This game is
Master of Orion.
Yes, I am one of those who played the original games years ago.
Ok, so it is not Master of Orion, but it is a good 4X space strategy.
This game feels more like a combination of Endless Space and Galactic Civilizations, with a very dull real-time combat where you cannot change the outcome much. Doesn't matter if you just watch the battle or command the ships yourself.
Now, the real-time combat can be done right. For example StarDrive 2 has significantly better real-time combat where you can actually change the tide of battle by moving the ships smart. Even Endless Spaces' autocombat system feels better than this.
So yes, this is the biggest problem for me with the game. It lacks the turn-based combat that made the original two Master of Orions so great, and it does the real-time combat all wrong. I can handle the changes in the travel system (star lanes like Endless Space) or the (way too) slow game pace, and the tedious espionage system. But the combat system is just.. meh.
However, I do like the game. The poor combat system does not kill ALL the fun for me. I enjoy the colonizing & research phase of the game.
If you like Endless Space, then you should get this game on sale. I do not think this game is worth its full price, but on sale? Definately.
If I had to give a rating, I'd say 7/10.
It's pretty good, but it's not great. And it's definately not Master of Orion.
They had the budget to hire well known voice actors; why didn't they hire Steve Barcia and Ken Burd to oversee the project? Maybe next time.

With an old IP like this, there are plenty of nostalgics to moan and groan over any little change, from what i have seen this team genuinely gives a♥♥♥♥♥♥about the franchise and has done a great job. I am still encountering some bugs, but usually a reboot will fix them.
Some things to note:
You can pause at any time to issue orders to move/attack, which are then carried out all at the same time when you hit 'play'. I think this is great, and gets around the issue in MoO2 where a large fleet would take forever to command. This also opens up options like having a horde of small expendable vessles rather than a few of the biggest ships available.
You will need to purchase DLC to play as the Elerian, Gnolam, or Trilarian races. I dont like that these races were excluded from the original game. A more palatable move would have been to have all the original races playable, and to invent some brand new races/traits as paid DLC
Some silly decisions by the devs are made moot with mods. e.g. having only 10 points to spend on your custom race, not being able to see/select all perks when making a custom race, Anarans being stupidly strong, (
)
The voice acting is great in my experience, but overused. Your advisor pops up all the time, and says one of about 5 lines every time you choose a technology to research. Thankfully there is an option to mute the advisor.
Unlike prior games, travel between the stars takes place via 'starlanes'. Each system has one or more point from which you can travel to another system. These points are the only place to enter or exit a system, and so become chokepoints you can block or defend with military instalations.
A major part of previous Orion games was researching fuel tech, to enable you to explore further. In Master of Orion there is no limit to the distance you are able to venture from your colonies. To make up for this, you must now explore each planet within a system to determine the size/biome/mineral/bonuses, meaning exploration is a more involved task.
Overall a very enjoyable game with mods, and getting better all the time.

Blood Bowl: Chaos Edition isn't much different from the Legendary Edition, though I understand most people recommend buying Chaos Edition if you haven't purchased either. They have some extra races included.
Blood Bowl is Games Workshop's blend of American Football and Rugby, and is a faithful recreation of the tabletop boardgame. Pick a race, recruit players, and have them all killed on the field by Chaos Dwarves during your first game.
BB is arbitrary, with good strategy only able to minimize the punishing dice rolls. Embrace the chaotic nature of your plans going awry, your Catcher with Sure Hands, Nerves of Steel, and Block dying at the hands of a zombie because you rolled 3 skulls and have no team re-rolls left, and watching a Gutter Runner go nearly the length of the entire field to score.
Because if you're lucky, you'll catch that little rat on the next play and break his neck, ending his career forever.
Not for the faint of heart or those who care that the dice are brutal and don't care about you.
For: people who enjoy NFL Blitz, watching Orcs beat down hapless Wood Elves, and anyone who can handle losing because the dice didn't go your way. Lots of fun.
Frustrating at times, but can be fun. Play as the Orcs.

THIS GAME IS VERY HARD! Sorry for the all caps, but that's what you need to know going into this. Unless you're the kind of person who can handle losing to the AI more often than not (even on Easy difficulty) don't bother with Blood Bowl. This game requires equal degrees of strategic brilliance and utter masochism to be enjoyed. Fans of the game insist the AI doesn't fudge dice rolls in its favor but I'm not so sure on that considering that the AI players almost always make successful dodge rolls regardless of Agility. But, even if it doesn't cheat, this is hardly a relaxing game experience and seems to be aimed at people who enjoy ungodly difficulty.
I really gave this game the best chance that I could, playing hotseat matched against myself until I was certain I understood the rules before moving on to play the AI. Ultimately I clocked in about 22 hours of play over the course of five days before deciding to request a refund. That's the other thing, even if the difficulty and very steep learning curve aren't a problem for you this game simply isn't worth the $30 price tag. I wish I could've enjoyed this game, it's very charming and you can tell the people who made it were fans of the original board game but (call me crazy) I think life is frustrating enough without something that's supposed to be for entertainment frustrating you further. This was the only time I've ever requested a refund from Steam based on a game's difficulty (every previous time was because the game had problems running) and this is the first Steam review I'm writing. That should give you an idea of how much Blood Bowl drove me up a wall.

"Serena" is a free to play, horror, adventure game. Don't expect cheap jumpscares, and freaky monsters running around dark halls. This is not what "Serena" is about. What it really is about, is a journey through a man's psyche.
The whole area of the game is confined to one, small, old, dusty cabin. And in this dark, cramped space you experience a man's thinking process. You walk around the cabin, looking at different pieces of equiment, furniture, clothes etc. The man slowly remembers the story of him, and his girl - Serena, drifting apart.
This game is an experience worth having. If you're expecting scares, well you will be dissapointed. But the mood is extremely creepy and sort of threatening, so I didn't feel like I was missing out on anything - even though I love horror.
It is unbelievably depressing, but also fascinating. To go through the stages of a person's thinking process. How this man goes through sadness, denial, longing, anger... all these emotions rushing through him in powerful waves. How one hair brush, or bottle of perfume can cause this many associations... This is something most of us have experience at one point or another, due to heartbreak. And it feels liberating to see others go through it so similarly.
And don't worry, the game isn't all just reminscing. There is a mystery. Why is he having trouble with his memory? Why is the atmosphere so disturbing? Where is Serena, and why is she gone? The ending might not be the most surprising thing ever, but it did send chills down my spine. The lack of music only enhances the feelings.
Plus, it's free, and going through the whole thing didn't even take me an hour, so even if you don't love it... you won't really lose anything. So I would suggest you give it a shot, and let yourself immerse in the unhappy outcome of a bad relationship. Experience "Serena".

Short but sweet! Well--heartbreaking would be a better way to describe it! Serena is a very haunting game and I couldn't stop playing until I knew the truth. And what a truth it was. Unexpected plot twists and the sad and romantic story make this one a winner for me.
Definitely recommended, and it's free! Give this game a try.

This is a weird game. It's sometimes very fun, and sometimes ridiculously boring and horrible.
To start off, the story is poor and almost non existent, with even worse voice acting to accompany the few cut scenes.
The levels are okay sometimes, but other times they take forever, especially when you have to sit there and figure out what you need to kill to pass the level. This takes even longer when certain enemies take certain spells to kill, but the enemies are never consistent. Sometimes you need to use fire, and later you many need to use lightning. All the while you are trying to figure this out, you are getting mobbed by never ending enemies.
Tat being said though, the game is at a comfortable difficulty, so its not really all that frustrating.
Though the most frustrating thing is the toughest enemies you will find in this game...pots. Dear god those pots. The hit detection is so horrendous, you will spend a good 30 seconds trying to break a pot. They seem to just break whenever they feel like it...it's so annoying.
Oh and rolling is horrendous too...yeah, rolling. Rolling is so hard and random to acheive that there are two levels dedicated to just managing to pull off rolling three times to beat the level. It's a disaster.
Jumping is a mess as well, though still easily doable.
Some good things about the game is the combat is ok, with plenty of upgrades and spells to keep things interesting. Other than spells, you can use swords and guns to attack foes, making for nice, varied gameplay. There are hidden artifacts in the levels to find too, which give you special upgrades.
The best part about the game though is your character, Ayumi. You get to enjoy the nice view of a woman clad only in underwear and a few shreds of armor, but even this does not distract from all the downsides of the game.
Overall its not the worst game I've ever played, not even close really, but it sure isn't good. I wouldn't recommend spending more than $2.00 on this

This game is quite relaxing and the art is unique, interesting, and gorgeous. There is a bit of a more random element to this game compared to other point and click adventure games, but I still really enjoyed it. I liked collecting all the creature cards and looking at the art. It does not do anything, but it's an interesting and creative little feature. Be prepared to run around a lot in confusingly mapped out levels. I liked the level design because it is different, however, even with the mini map I did get lost a few times.
I would recommend purchasing this game in a bundle or on sale since it does have a limited amount of playthrough, and is short. I finished it within six hours, but I am going to go back and get the rest of the achievements later so if you play games like me (extremely slowly) you will get your money's worth. One tip that might be obvious to other people but it took me a while to figure out is when you have an item in your inventory you can only apply it in the room it is supposed to be applied to. So, if you go to take it out of your inventory and it does not budge then you know it is not needed in that room. That feature definitely made figuring out the puzzles easier for me.
In conclusion, if you enjoy relaxing, atmospheric, slower-paced, random, point and click adventure games I would highly recommend. If you are the kind of player that wants to play a game that is fast-paced this is not the game for you.

Randomly, you might have to repeat the above an arbitrary number of times until some other arbitrary things happen.  Also, be warned that you cannot go back to previous levels of the game without restarting.  So, if you manage to miss something optional (i.e., for an Achievement), happen to have everything necessary to finish the level, and click on the thing that finishes the level, you're SOL.  Using a walk-through, I managed to drag my way through level 4 of the game's 6 levels.  Looking at what was in level 5, I threw up my hands in disgust and quit (and I'm a completionist).  If you're one of the people who like other Amanita Design games, you'll probably love this one.  But, for the rest of us, just no.  Not Recommended.

Darkouts reviews are mixed because of angry backers who were promised content that had to be scrapped from the original project. They have a right to be upset... However the developer does actually want to add that content in the future, but it will be released as Paid DLC. The other source of negative reviews are those with early access bugs... Don't let these people stop you from experiencing something fun and different. At first glance they nearly disuaded me as well and I am very happy I ignored their rage and tried it for myself.
The game itself is really amazing the art style is just gorgeous and light mechanics are very unique. Having light as a battle mechanic gives a small but considerable degree of strategy to your base designs and how you handle combat. The Darkness itself can be interesting as it conceals enemies and resources and allows enemies to spawn undetected. This creates gameplay that draws you in because your constantly on alert making sure nothing jumps you. In contrast something like Terraria all enemies on screen are known and obvious... I think the darkness and the unknown makes the game more fun and I have yet to experience this in any other similar games of this genre.
There is a text based mission style tutorial, and its not as hard as people say. Follow the directions, read, and you will be fine once the first five minutes pass you should have a pretty good idea of how to handle invintory, your hotbars, controls and they even give you flares and a lamp, and gun to start off with. Crafting is not difficult once you get the hang of it either. Honestly I love how you have to discover how to create things for yourself. Oh look you found a vine? Lets learn to craft this into rope. Oh you have rope? Lets learn to craft this other thing... Its wonderful and I much prefer that to the terraria style of crafting where "I magically know everything somehow"
The enviornment itself sustains you. Learning to hunt the shadow creatures and various glowing wildlife allows you to heal. You can be creative and sculpt locations for these creatures to thrive. Your home base also becomes a safe location during the moon phases. Darkmoons are long periods of near pitch black conditions where enemies spawn much more rapidly. Being caught away from home during one of these moon phases can be particularily unpleasant.
As you can see from a single player experience there is a strong push towards a slightly more immersive style gameplay both in terms of crafting, exploration, and moment to moment combat in the darkness. The beautiful artwork and lighting effects also adds to this sensation as well.
The game is very much Sandbox right now. Story isn't 100% completed but you still can find audio logs from survivors who have died long before you arived, broken shelters, debris and other signs of previous human activity hidden in the game. Its very interesting and if this sounds like something you would enjoy trying then help the developer and purchase the game and make your own opinon about where it stands at this time.

A cute point-and-click puzzle game about a group of plant-like friends on a quest to save their home from an invasion of parasitic creatures. Progressing through the game usually relies on the characters finding certain items, which you collect by solving small situational puzzles like picking the right character to solve a problem, beating an NPC at a minigame, or manipulating the environment in some fashion. The biggest challenge in these usually comes from which mechanic to rely on (i.e. clicking on an item vs. clicking
it vs. click-and-drag), but that doesn’t detract too much from the game. Part of this may stem from the absence of dialogue and text, but I think it was the right stylistic choice to add to the game’s charm. The world, art style, and tone all play off one another well, making it fun just to take your time and click around each screen to see what you might unearth. Recommended for fans of puzzle games and anyone who wants a game that encourages them to slow down and give their mind a light challenge.

As a big fan of this series it's no surprise that I would endorse. This game is more in the spirit of MOO 2 which was most fun of the first three (my opinion). I feel that this game is even more fun. There are two areas of gameplay that stand out to me as fundamentaly different than MOO 2: Spying and Movement.
Spying in MOO 2 was very simple. Produce spies in the building que then send your spies in the diplomacy screen to steal tech or destroy infrastructure. In this game however your spies are not made through production, they are rather trained (once unlocked) giving you one at a time. There are more specific options on how you wish to afflict your opponent, such as causing a food shortage leaving your potental conquest more fruitful than simply destroying random buildings.
Movement in MOO2 was simply distance limit from your closest colony or outpost. In this game the junction points that connect the systems offer you a more "front line" way of thinking than constantly worrying that your oppenent is going Ender's Game on you by sending his ships directly toward your home planet. That strategic reality is not nessesarily better, just different.

As a long-time fan of the Master of Orion series, I'll admit was I pretty hesitant about picking up this remake/reboot/whatever you want to call it. Some of the decisions made by the devs didn't sit well with me at all, but I finally decided to give the game a fair go.
Before I start - I'm reviewing MOO + the Antares DLC, and I'm running the 5X mod. These both impact my overall impression of the game.
I'm happy to say that my experiences with the game so far have been mostly positive. I loved the turn-based combat of the original MOO series, but I have to admit that running battles in real-time allows for a fairer outcome, rather than the "wipe-the-opposite-fleet-off-the-map-before-they-get-a-chance-to-shoot" scenarios I quite often had in MOO2, and was almost always able to take advantage of in the late-game.
The overhaul of the espionage system with the DLC was a definite step in the right direction.
This might not be the MOO that hard-core fans wanted, but this is definitely the most fun I've had in a space-based 4X game since the days of MOO2. There are aspects I'm not entirely fond of, such as star-lanes, the Antaran's obesession with me in every game, the mod menu working whenever it decides it wants to, and the fact that I have to make use of a mod to get a decent balanced game.
There are bugs that crop up from time to time, and the game tends to slow down pretty drastically as you get closer to your turn-limit. I tend to let the AI take care of space battles because once there are enough ships on the screen managing all of them becomes a massive pain.
If you had to ask me whether I would recommend the game - I would say yes. It's not everything I hoped for, but it ticks most of the right boxes for me, personally. There are still many areas in which the game can improve, and hopefully the devs will work on some of these.
If reading this review still doesn't make you decide one way or another, I'd recommend waiting for the next sale, and grabbing it then.

It's a simple aerial dogfighting. You basically try to fulfill the map objective. There is a free-for-all deathmatch where you try to be the first to get 10 kills, there is a goal scoring map where you try to get your team to 6 goals, there is a bombing map where you collect a nuke to drop on your enemy's base. These are all first person shooter objectives from games like Quake and Unreal Tournament. Relative to other games on the market, it's nothing much. However, the game is simple enough that you can easily pick up the game. You accelerate and decelerate with the Up and Down keys respectively, and you point the direction with the mouse. Attack is Left Click, Launch Object is Middle Click and Special is Right Click.
Conclusion, try it but it's not a big winner.

Man, I really wanted to like this game.  I played through and beat the last X-Com game with little fanfare, sure it had it's moments but Jesus is this a step up in difficulty.  One of the things I found really frustrating is that the early game enemies start with mind control and got to experience it first had on the first mission of the game. So right out the gate I lose one of the four members of my team with no recourse. I understand this game is supposed to be hard but punish me for things I do wrong, not just randomness.
This would be fine if it wasn't for the larger issue at hand, the timers. I'm all for being the scrappy underdog and losing guys along the way, hell, the playthrough in the first game I lost loads of guys on missions.  The timers in this game are in basically every mission which seems incredibly counterintuitive when you are supposed to be stealthy and cautious.  So what am I supposed to do, rush the objective or set up an ambush, I cannot do both.
I am sure there are plenty out there who will lambast me for not being good enough, but again, I played and beat the first game, nothing here is new but I got my♥♥♥♥♥♥♥kicked.  I'm fine with this, I love Dark Souls after all but this game honestly feels really cheap.  If it isn't mind control, it's enemies who see me across the map or snakes pulling my guys across the map.  Naturally these are all abilities given no explanation as why would they announce them, but the issue here as I mentioned earlier is that these abilities are incredibly lethal.  So on top of trying to be as stealthy as possible due to a timer, early cheap enemy abilities, and cutscenes constantly freezing my game so people can tell me things I already know I find it to be a very grating experience. I tried, I really tried.
Now it's not all bad, the whole sword thing is great, as are some of the upgrades (swords that stun? yes please), but the game is stressful and exhausting.  The difficulty feels cheap, the pace is exhausting (timers and people constantly yelling at you) and you don't really have time to actually ENJOY the game.
There are some cool ideas but timers do not mix with stealth, they just don't.  Have all the doom clocks you want but not everything needs to autodestruct.  At least not right away, you could easily have made many of those timers dark events.  Make them something the player would want to spend time/resources to counteract.  As I said earlier, I really want to like this game but it's entirely too stressful for the payoff.

As a turn-based strategy game, XCOM2 has done well in overall. Its imbalance in enemies and time-limit design make the game more challenging, forcing players to plan the movement more carefully and sometimes more risky. In personnel, I quite enjoy this kind of challenge, if there is no RNG factor.
In comparison to XCOM:EU, XCOM2 requires a better resource planning in the beginning. Or, you will pay your debt during progression because your enemies will always outperform you in "hardware". To work around, you need stronger weapons to set up a plan, eliminating a group of enemies within one turn.
The only one thing frustrates me is RNGesus in this game. You want to hack for battle advantages? RNG. You want to hit your enemies? RNG. You want to finish your scanning before raids? RNG. You want to win a battle certainly? 100% chance to hit your every enemies or pray RNGesus. This issue also exists in XCOM:EU, but it's not very annoying since you can resolve with sufficient preparation before hands. In XCOM2, imbalance in forces and time-limit will teach you lessons, unless you install mods to mitigate them.

This is a rather good mystery suspense game that puts you into the shoes of a man trying to figure out his life. His wife left him at some point and he tries to find out exactly what happened and why she would leave. It gets to the point where he wonders if all his memories are just figments of a dream. It plays on the psychological aspect of mystery to where there is no actual danger, but your mind can actually start to panic. I actually started to panic along with the character slightly with how intense the story was getting.
It’s a very simple game when you talk in terms of gameplay, just point and click to get into the different items around you or to move around the cabin. Now as you play, you have to click on pretty much everything or else you may not get to the next part of the story, a thing I was trying to figure out and almost didn’t finish the story without looking at a walkthrough. It is real easy to get stuck if you don’t try every little thing and you might have to click on things more then once. There are also audio cues as well you have to listen for as well. So many little things can make the game play a nightmare when stuck.
The textures are very dark and dirty, making it feel slightly like a horror game. There are dark pictures around the cabin that are slightly hard to see but it feels like it’s a very old place. The texture work makes everything very realistic, almost too much texture in some areas, but you can tell something is slightly off. I don’t really get it but its like the lines around everything is a little to crisp and clean to be real.
The voice acting and the music is rather gentle and fits with the whole style of the game. The sad man speaking and narrating his story fits with the sad almost non existent sound. This is really a quiet game. You get music only minimally leaving the haunting impression that makes this game an interesting game to play through.
It is short, sweet and even though sometimes hard to play for a first timer (as sometimes I could not find what would set the next section off) it was a nice short game. It’s free to play on steam right now.

This game is such a letdown.
On paper Tower Unite sounds incredibly fun; playing games with your friends, earning currency to purchase cosmetics and furniture, decorating your condo, etc. Essentially the social aspect of the game is what makes it fun for me. Constantly playing Mini-Golf or Virus (because these are the only populated games usually) does get boring after a while.
Sadly, this isn't enough to keep the game alive. The 12 developers, supposed "full time" (Monday-Friday, 10 AM - 6 PM) work at a soulcrushingly slow rate. The updates they do release are usually barren of content or outright useless (rollercoaster).
They also appear to have their priorities wrong; one example is working on parental controls (which again, is being worked on incredibly slowly) that no one really needs right now. Another example is furniture, but guess what; it's only rocks, trees and plants. Not tables or anything like it. I feel like they have too many projects going on at once which may explain the slow rate of content being produced.
What the game needs is content, even new cosmetics or furniture added regularly would help keep the game alive by giving players something to work towards. Right now I don't see this game moving forward because of the disorganized and inefficient development cycle.
If you visit the SteamCharts page for Tower Unite, you can see that the player population is dwindling despite having around 130k owners (as of October 2017), again indicating a lack of interest in the game due to the lack of content. Player retention is going down the gutter because of this, and it's a real shame.
To the developers, I ask you to spend some time considering what the players want or get rid of the dead weight because there is no way 12 "full time" developers can work at such an abysmal rhythm.

This game is a blast to play, both with friends and just solo with strangers. I was super excited to play it when I first came across it and saw a couple of my favorite youtubers playing it, but I read the reviews and they mostly said that no one plays this game anymore. That statement was happily disproven by me when I finally decided to just go ahead and get it. Although you have to play and the New York servers, the playerbase behind this game are a really funny bunch. Always getting into something or another. And the customizations you can do to your condo and other things are superb.
The minigames are great, although I don't feel like they were crafted in a way that allows them to take as many rounds as they do. Basically you might end up playing Virus longer than you opted for. But hey, more credits amirite?
And that's the other thing, credits. I love the way these are handed out in this game. You always get the consolation, "Thanks for playing" credits at the end of the round. And then afterwards, depending on if you were on the losing or winning team, or how well you did in the round, you get credits for that score. But even on the losing team, (i.e. the ghosts on the little squires game,) you get credits, just not as much. This makes the game feel less like a grind, and more like a Mario party that comes with a customizable condo.
Like I said before, the game also has a Super Sluggers kinda hub vibe to me, by which I mean if you're not either in a minigame or your condo, there's tons to do in the plaza inbetween grinding and such. This game is never a dull moment.
Overall, if you're teetering on the edge of buying this game, I'd say buy it, wait for someone to finally speak up on mic, and I guarantee you whatever they say will be so incredibly stupid and funny you'll want to stay for the entire ride.

One would expect Master of Orion (4), to take best elements of 1, 2 and 3 (yes there were plenty of good mechanics in MOO3) and put them together to create the best 4X space game ever. Unfortunately, anyone who expected so, overestimated the goals that apparently developers and publishers had. The game is pretty much a copy-paste of mechanics from MOO2 (and MOO1 by inference) with pretty graphics (which is undisputably good). The issue I see is that superior mechanics from MOO3 were not even partially implemented here. Don't get me wrong - MOO3 was far from being perfect, but it contained some of the very novelty and complex mechanics that improved the immerssion of empire management and gave feeling that you must explore the game also allowing one to use new features quite intuitively. The only poorly executed part of MOO3 - real time combat was in fact introduced to MOO(4), but so far it is as plain and boring as it was in the infamous precedessor (although with correct 3D field and perspective this time).
It amazes me that having access to all code and IP for all 3 MOOs, developers decided to create Master of Orion 2.5 all over again. Instead of taking on the vision of an ultimate 4X game that this game could be, they apparently decided to lower the ceiling and gave us same old stuff that everyone knows and which cannot possibly fail...
Hey Devs - are you going to do a proper Master of Orion 4? If you cannot - get someone who will.

So i purchased this game back in beta and played it a bit, I leave my games open on steam when I'm sleeping and such, so I've played it about 1/3 what my profile shows.  That's still enough to get a good feel for the game.  Back then I stopped playing because there were some pretty game breaking bugs when you got far down the tech tree and the story was almost non existent and what was there was pretty buggy.  So I stopped playing to wait for the game to be finished, quite happy with my taste of the game and looking forward to the full version.  I've checked on it a few times since then, but now it's been over a year and I find this... the game will never be finished.  They released it without finishing all the things that I was promised and want more money for DLC that will finish the game.  Considering how badly they've neutered themselves with this move, it's more likely they will never make this DLC anyway.  To top it all off, they complain that the reason is people buying it on steam sale... well I'm pretty sure I bought it at full price, I remember something like $14.99, because I believe in supporting indie games and I could afford it at the time.  Insulting players who couldn't afford or didn't want to pay that much is just wrong.  Having said that, I paid $14.99 for a game that will never be finished and has the same features set as games you can get for 4.99-9.99... Now I don't mind that per se, but I spent that money expecting the features that were promised, I may have been able to afford the game, but I'm not rich, that 14.99 could buy me a game that I will actually enjoy, because I'll never get to play this game for 100s of hours like I wanted to when it was finally finished. That being said, below is my review on the parts of the game that exist.
Pros:
*Very nice aesthetic, lighting effects and such.  For a 2-D game it's quite beautiful.
*Interesting Research and fun building, you can do some cool stuff farther up the tech tree
*This game can suck up a good deal of time, it's addictive to a point, but there's a limit
Cons:
*Game becomes repetitive after awhile, mostly due to lack of content, there's plenty of sandbox building, but not much else
*Game is still relatively buggy, and world files can actually become corrupted, forcing you to start on a new world
*Story may as well not exist, the story elements are boring, there are no real quests or missions, every bit of it is basically "go find these capsules that have your quest items in it and then come back and put them in your satelite dish.
*ORIGINAL PROMISES NOT MET - that's the killer for me right there.

Amazing game. The combat is fast and engaging, with tons of different weapon combinations and abilities. The enemies can be quite challenging, especially if you pick the optional challenges, but the pacing is very good and I never considered any level especially unfair. It's not without it's flaws, though. Some of the more effective weapons can get downright boring, and once you find a good weapon and fully upgrade it, the game just becomes easy. This actually led me to quit the game for over a year, although my general dislike for hack-and-slash combat probably had something to do with it. I did warm up to it on my later playthrough, and if you ever think the game is too easy, try turning on ALL the challenges and prepare for pain. To give you an idea, these challenges make them tougher, stronger, faster, regenerate health, slow you on hit, randomly turn invulnerable, randomly ignore your attacks, and most importantly, make them stop dropping health potions, as well as all other random potion drops. Not so easy now, huh?
The story is just spectacular. The story itself is rather simple, and it's quite short only lasting about 6 hours, if you take the optional missions. But the combination of a beautiful artstyle; stellar voice-acting, even from characters who only get a few lines in the game; and an absolutely stunning soundtrack; makes these six hours one of the best experiences I've had in a game.
I cannot describe just how beautiful this game is. I can't even describe all the things it did well, because it did everything well.  The music, the artstyle, the voice-acting, all of it is done so well, and works together so well. It really has to be experienced, and with the rather low price, I'd recommend you to buy this game if you have any interest in one of the most beautiful games I have ever played.
