I was a huge fan of the original Master Of Orion and MOO 2, and for many years I have been hoping for a decent reboot (MOO 3 was terrible). I'm very happy to be able to say I've found it.
I was wary of this one due to the number of poor reviews. Thankfully, I thoroughly enjoyed it. I feel that the negative reviews are mostly in relation to early issues which have since been patched out. Some seem to have expected something this reboot never promised to be.
If you enjoyed the original version of MOO 1 and 2, then you will find this to be fairly true to source with some nicely updated graphics. However, be aware that the genre has evolved somewhat since the originals. Newer releases such as Stellaris include a fair amount of complexity and variation, whereas this retains the majority of the original gameplay. In comparison, MOO seems streamlined and simplified in comparison, although from me this isn't a complaint.
I began playing with high expectations and was not disappointed. The layout is at once polished yet familiar, with all of the character and style of the original. The diplomacy plays out as well as I remembered, with some nice voice acting and animations to really give each race their own personality. The combat has made the switch to real time with pause, and varying levels of control depending on your preference.
I have thoroughly enjoyed  my first 12 hours or so returning to the MOO galaxy, and I expect there will be many more to come.

TL;DR: This is the first actual MoO2 remake that's both faithful and modern.
I'm an old-school MoO fan, having played hundreds of hours of both MoO and MoO2. No 4X since MoO2 has captured me like that game did, because they all made fundamental mistakes or oversights.
I did not have high hopes for this game, because the previews looked bad, but I was very, very pleasantly surprised. This game actually does have the MoO2 spirit, and almost all of the important stuff is there. The radical race differences, the simple yet effective economy, the ship design, the battles - it's all there. Some of it is streamlined, in particular the battles, but for the most part the important bits are intact.
If I had to complain, it would be that they went slightly too far in the streamlining of the tactical battles. Realtime is fine, there's a wide variety of weapons and modules, and taking control of the battle does make a difference (particularly whenever torpedoes are involved), but I just wish they would have kept the shield quadrants, the subsystem damage and the ability to board ships.
Other than that minor complaint, this game is great. Aggressive AI, a big and interesting tech tree with almost all the old MoO2 techs, hugely different races (telepathic and tolerant is out, but lithovore and creative is still in!), all in a very polished and neat package. Definitely recommended.

I've loved every Master of Orion game, including Master of Orion 3 (a game I feel gets a worse rap than it deserves) and this one. But I cannot recommend it to anyone else.
If you're a fan of prior Master oF Orion games, playing this raises a lot of fun little nods to them. Everything from the reprised races from old games to the fact that the colonization music is the same tune as its MS-DOS ancestor. The people that made this game definitely knew the Master of Orion series.
Other reviewers here have brought up very valid points, however, regarding how this doesn't embody the spirit of Master of Orion. No free range travel, making various drives and fuels boring and inconsequential, overall simpler. Star lanes make things very isolated, and present a very different, in a much simpler way. Technology tree is very straight forward, even if you've got the illusion of choice, you're very likely to just be picking the same tech everyone else is, and unlike the prior games you eventually can just research everything (outside of very VERY few technology categories where you pick what effect it has and have to trade with another empire that picked the other), overall the science track is much simpler. Combat is very straight forward, with none of the dynamics of missile counter measuring, and all the jazz with boarding ships with tractor beams or assault shuttles, making for a simpler tactical battle altogether.
You'll notice a common theme, here... Everything's simple. Very... Easy to grasp and just click through without much thought or care.
That's when I realized the real issue I have with this Master of Orion reboot. And why I also still enjoy it. It's simple. Easy. And really is just a lot of playful references to the older games.
Presently, I just play the game when I'm on downtime at work, or need to break the monotony of studying. But if I want to truly sit down and enjoy a game? I'd sooner just go for Master of Orion 2. This game sooner belongs on a tablet or cell phone, with how simple it is, and I'm seriously wondering if that's the idea they had at the start.
Overall, I enjoy the game. But if you want a real TBS experience, I'll much sooner recommend ANY other Master of Orion game. I'd only recommend this if you've got a laptop and barely have an hour or two to kill in a very simple 4x Strategy game that probably should've been made a tablet game.

For it's price Blackwake is a delightful early access multiplayer title.  If you enjoyed Black Flag but wanted a more hands on experience this may be the game for you.  Currently there are two types of ships a smaller schooner type vessel and a galleon with smaller crew sizes on the schooner and larger ones on the galleon.  The game shines exceptionally if you get a captain and crew that works together, and can become significantly interesting in multiple ship battle modes with captains coordinating with each other.
The crew are absolutely vital and have a number of responsibilities they must complete in order to be victorious and these include:  manually loading cannons with a variety of different shots, repairing holes and sails, manning the pumps when sinking, and manning the swivels.  The captain typically drives the ship and relays orders but can jump down and help out the crew if they need to.
There are boarding actions which require you to fire grapple shots to hook the enemy ship.  Additionally, you can ram an enemy vessel, but this will immobilize your own ship in the process until it is repaired.
Currently there is only one type of game mode which is team death match with a few different options to play it.  Either with just small vessels, or a mixture of large and small vessels.
There is the beginnings of a progressions system in terms of different cosmetic looks the higher you go in levels.  Currently there are no better weapons for leveling, but there is a variety of weapons which include muskets, blunderbuss, a hand cannon that shoots bombs, varieties of pistols, and a variety of melee weapons.
Perhaps one of the more interesting aspects is that the all the weapons have extensive loading times similar to how they would in real life.  The handheld weapons all have well done reload animations that justify why exactly it is taking so long to reload.  As a result of the loading time you essentially get one shot with your musket and pistol before needing to switch to your sword during intense boarding actions.
Despite realistic loading animations there are some comically unrealistic elements.  For instance if your boat is sinking water will begin to flood the ship, but never fear because you can breathe underwater!  That's right, there is no breath meter so you can stay underwater for ever to repair and man the pumps.  Ships can still be sunk even with this "feature" so don't worry.
As typical with early access games optimization is lacking in some areas, but overall the game runs decently and all of the major game functions do work.  The server browser needs some improvement such as better filters, but it is satisfactory for now.  Joining a server is confusing at first because there is nothing indicating what is happening until it either throws you back to the browser or actually puts you in the game.  Melee combat is a little floaty and will hopefully feel more precise and solid as the game develops.  There are no cross hairs on any of the weapons so you are pretty much eyeballing shots in many cases.  The only weapon which will let you aim to some degree are the musket type weapons with their iron sights.  Finally it would be nice to have some type of hit indicator for melee and ranged weapons to determine and something to see where the bullets are actually going.
Overall it is a very enjoyable experience and requires a significant amount of teamwork to pull off victories at sea.
Definitely a game worth playing. Just from the experience that this has given me, I'd regularly buy content from the developer.

Ingredients
1 cup Country Crock®
¾ cup packed brown sugar
¾ cup granulated sugar
1 large egg
1 large egg yolk
2 tsp. vanilla extract
3 cups all-purpose flour
1 tsp. baking powder
¾ tsp. salt
¼ tsp. baking soda
1 to 2 cups of your choice of mix-ins
Directions
Preheat oven to 375°. Mix brown sugar, granulated sugar, Country Crock spread, egg, egg yolk and vanilla into a large bowl until well mixed. Stir in flour, baking powder, salt and baking soda until blended (dough will be soft and creamy).
Add mix-ins (such as chocolate chips, sprinkles, nuts, dried fruit, etc.) into the dough until every spoonful of dough has some of the delicious mix-ins.
Drop dough by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets 3-inches apart. Bake 10 to 12 minutes until edges are lightly golden. Cool 1 minute on wire rack; remove from baking sheets and cool completely.

I just took the weekend for 2 of Amanita's games: Machinarium and Botanicula.
If you've ever played Machinarium before (and you liked it), I'm telling you now that Botanicula is just as amazing. Get it, play it, enjoy it! The graphics are lighter and more colourful in general, the puzzles are only a little less challenging (so no need for a "cheating" notebook on the upper right corner, but you still need to crack your head every once in a while), and the story is just as adorable.
If you haven't played any of this studio's games, however, allow me to summarise without spoiling you: Botanicula tells the story of a group of plant-y friends who embark on a journey to save the tree of light from darkness (embodied by spiders). Since it's a puzzle game, you need to complete several tasks to get items and continue to the next level. You will find a total of 123 creatures, each representing a creature card that will be given to you, and which you can look at by selecting the deck on the upper left corner. Take your time, though! There are plenty of Easter eggs along the way (golden cards, and also your Steam achievements) that don't all need to be found for you to go through to the end.
100% recommend if you're into logic and thinking while having fun.

The game crashed on me because of a faulty audio file that wouldn't work, but was able to bypass it. A lot of the 'gameplay' is figuring out which way is the right way to go with little to no direction, the worst of this being two sections where you crawl through vents. The only encounter with a 'stalker' type thing is a flipping QTE sequence. Game is stupidly dark sometimes, you have a flashlight, but a draining battery pushes you to conserve batteries and lurk in the dark. Not fun to explore sometimes, and the game punished you for it sometimes, such as a scene where exploring can end up with you locked into a death scene with a train hitting you, and then having to start the game all over. However, game does have some nice lighting in places, the atmosphere in parts is pretty good, there's one or two moments that I feel were well handled (a scene later in involving a window pops up in my mind), most of it isn't offensively bad, just kind of ehh. Game ends abruptly on a cliffhanger "TO BE CONTINUED...".

This game feels a bit like MOO for console.  Everything has been "dumbed down"
The game is resonable well polished, looks good, few bugs and It would probably stand up 10 years ago.
It stands up well on its own if you have never played a 4x and don't compare it to anything.
but the 4x genre has moved on, other games leave this feeling dated and incomplete.
Its sad to see a game that defined the 4x for years get released like this.
I find myself watching TV while playing this game.
Issues
The tech tree is very repetative with no real innovation, just 25% more +1 dmg and you don't really decide what to research you just work along the tree.   Often attepting to pickup just production and planet techs, researches everything; guns, shields etc there is no way to focus a "tree" like other games.
All races share the same tech tree and have very little variation in racial traists outside 25% bonus in X to make them unique.  The one race that doesn't consume food (like every 4x these days) is the only Unique trait.
The AI is hideously dumb and not very agressive, You have to try to provoke combat in most situations and then its simply a matter of defeating 2-3 fleets and GG you won. now you spend 50+ turns playing Whack-a-Mole on planets that spawn a single frigate.  The game "ends" in 1-2 turns of combat.
Increasing AI difficulty simply makes them cheat and build faster.
There is no real tactical depth, the Combat is very simple, the area you fight in is too small to play ranged tactics and ships respond poorly to commands, about the only tactics involved is making sure missile vollys don't overkill small ships.
The "ship builder" is the most simplistic thing I have seen in almost any 4x that basically boils down to, do you want direct fire weapons or missiles and upgrade your ships armor/shields x% every tech level.
Unlike most games where a well built design can outclass multiple designs of the same production value this game feels like you simply pick what colour the lines seen in combat will be.
Govening is poor, when you get a large amount of planets its quickly annoying to spam production, the game stops after a build queue of 4 as if we are saving memory space for consoles? Autobuild seems to randomly pick somthing, there is no large scale tools and managing fleets is just annoying.
I feel like the developers of this game need to play some "MOO clones" and implement all the innovation and amazing features that have been developed over the past 10 years.
It feels more like a High rez texture pack for an old game

MOO4 is a nice return to the franchise.  It really plays very similar to MOO2, without the Antarians attacking randomly.
The micromanaging of your colonies is made fairly easy via the way events are presented each turn.
MOO4, which by the way, I really wish the folks behind the game just called it MOO4 to avoid confusion.  It's ok to have lots of sequels, look at Final Fantasy!  Anyway, MOO4 swaps out the MOO2-turn based space combat engine to a RTS style engine found in any other game of this genre.  The cinematic camera in the space combat is annoyingly bad, with no way to control camera, or battle.  Top down seems the best way to watch space battles and naturally it never ceases to entertain to watch large fleets unleash death upon each other.
Overall MOO4 feels and plays a lot like MOO2 in my opinion.  It doesn't really bring much new to the table in terms of comparison to MOO2, but at least it's copying from a proven game.  All the familiar races and elements, right down to the types of random events feels taken straight from MOO2.
It gets my thumbs up, because it's just as fun as MOO2, but I gotta say, I hope this series evolves if they plan to offer addons or another game (MOO5.)  If you liked MOO2, it's almost certain you'll like this, it's nearly the same game.

It's getting there. I purchased StarBound a while back even though I was skeptical  about the game. This was due to the fact that many people were complaining that the game never received updates and was too similar to Terraria. However, shortly after I purchased the game, the updates started coming in--and more to come. It's a fun game with lot's to do. The building is great if your the decorative type and underground sections are much more interesting than in Minecraft. This game is still very much a beta, with only 3 boss battles. However, I have no doubt that as time goes on this number will increase.

+ The gameplay is fun and very unique for a platformer. You are essentially control a wisp like entity and can thrust upwards and downwards while trying to avoid walls or colored objects which cause you harm.
+ Visutally I find this game to be stunning. Very intriguing backgrounds with depth while having a very clean colorful minimalist aesthetic. Very soothing to the eye
+ The level design in this game really stands out to me. Each level is unique and tries to incorporate new or different mechanics on each and every stage that really keeps things interesting, entertaining, and fun. I kept wondering what would come next, and never wanted to put down the controller. Nothing felt repetitive, very creative!
+ Bonus objectives encourage replayability but are not mandatory. To get the trophy for each stage you need to beat the clock under a certain time, collect all the orbs, and refrain from hitting any colored blocks. (which can be challenging)
+ Quite a lot of content with 80 levels across 8 environments
- This is more of a personal thing, but I really wished there was more of a story. I kept wondering 'what am I? Where am I going? What will I find at the end?"

Not the most serious or grandest of games, but in the end I did find it enjoyable and worth it, and no, I'm not influenced by Ayumi's assets, not in the slightest, not at all....ok yes maybe!
Most levels are nice and short so you don't have to spend hours and hours over a level; think more like 10 minutes a level, and maybe 15-20 for the harder ones. For some people, this may be a con, but not everyone has all the free time to spend as others do.
Another bit of a con is that her voice is rather annoying when she speaks; it doesn't quite match the character at all.
In the end though, I enjoyed the game. It's a nice slasher game and the music and visuals aren't half bad either. I would recommend though that you buy it on sale.
Some useful tips though for new players:
- There is a good and a bad ending which is influenced by your "decisions". What is not hinted at all is that there "decisions" are not conversation based choices but rather based on the Spells/Abilities that you choose to learn (broad hint, "bad" spells have a colour/description that is rather obvious in hindsight). So be warned, if you want the good ending, hold off a bit until you have the choice of the "good" magics. You'll know by the name. Try not to end up like me who reached almost halfway before realising this and had to start all over because I wanted the good ending.
- Check your Beastiary often; it can be a huge help when countering some of the harder enemies.
- You have to spend souls on upgrades and whilst you may feel to be cheap in your spending, don't worry, you'll have plenty extra by then end of the game, and those upgrades to Regeneration and Form Duration are well worth the cost.
- And speaking of souls, you can also find them in breakable items, like statues and pots. And the items can also hide valuable upgrade parts/artifacts. So take the time to slash/shoot everything you can.
- There is also an area where you get an outfit upgrade, but, if you like how she looks, you can choose to not take it....because it covers more, lol
- The nice thing with dying is that you'll restart the level with all the enemies respawned but with all the souls and upgrades that you died with.
- There was one item of note, a scroll that halved the cost of any item/upgrade. The bad part, well you don't have a choice of whether to use it or not, it is automatically used on your very next purchase. Lets say you've been saving it for that (otherwise very costly) upgrade/spell, and you're in a fight and need to heal, well guess what, if you buy a heal, then say goodbye scroll. So better to use it before a fight so you can make your best choice.
- There are a few areas that involve jumping around. What can help is after you jump (or double jump) is to start shooting (or slashing). It slows down your descent and can help to extend the distance you cover while "falling". Really useful in some areas to get to hard to reach items or ledges. I recommend shooting over slashing however, as there is the chance that you do a special slash move that makes you move downwards....and maybe plummet to your death.
- In her special forms, her movement and attack speed increases, so make good use of it in those harder levels. I also noticed that her Rage (i.e. mana) may have taken longer to deplete when using abilities.

An amusing Visual Novel with rpg elements, or an amusing rpg with VN style cutscenes?
You decide.
There are a load of entertaining video game parodies in Antagonist. There’s ‘Loud,’ a spiky yellow haired hero with a giant boom box sword and headphones. There’s ‘Pink,’ the hero of time, with her ‘quadforce.’ There’s ‘Chefiroth,’ a silver haired chef’s hat wearing villain.
And several others. I won’t spoil them all here, but they’re very amusing.
There are basically two endings to the game and I’ve only gotten one. It’s pretty short and I enjoyed it, but I’ve heard the second ending is much more difficult to get on account of the final boss being almost impossible to kill.
I can see how that could happen, actually. The battle system is at first pretty straightforward, but unlike most rpgs, you can’t grind enemies to level up on your own. You will face an exact number of enemies in each playthrough and your levels, stats, and abilities are very much predetermined for each fight.
What changes are the skills you use and what basically comes down to luck in the turn order. Your AI partner will follow a semi-random attack pattern, which if you lucky enough to get in a turn right after they do, you can pick the same move they do, and you’ll both do a combination attack which is much better than most of the things you can do on your own. However, the AI will not match their attacks with yours and the chain is interrupted by enemy attacks, making this mechanic extremely random.
You can’t buy gear, so you’re best off to buy about twenty to thirty potions and spend the rest of your money on revives.
During my first playthrough, I only encountered a couple of fights where I had serious difficulty, and that was mostly due to multiple enemies repeatedly attacking one character or the other during the fight. This is rather hard to defend against.
On the whole, Antagonist has a fairly entertaining story, marred by somewhat troublesome combat mechanics. A single playthrough will probably take you a couple hours and the price is pretty good for the content you get, so I’m recommending it.
Oh, but don’t hit the F12 key. The steam overlay does NOT work and hitting F12 is the default key for dumping you back into the main menu without saving.
My only other complaint about the game is the blip beeping noise it makes with the text. You can hit a button to display it all at once, but that makes all the blips happen at the same time, which sounds very strange. Should be an option to turn off the text blip noises.

Despite its problems, it is the most fun I 've had in a Space 4x game in years.
Summary
Pros:
-Great UI design
-Interesting and memorable race design and graphics with top voice acting
-Great soundtrack and sound effects
-Warp Lanes allow for strategic gameplay
-Impessive tactical combat, especially once larger ships are unlocked
-Low price
-Accessibility & Workshop support
Cons:
-Some bugs
-No Scoreboard/Hall of Fame
-Somewhat uninteresting mid-game
-Mediocre AI
Let's get into the details...
I used to play Master of Orion 2 when I was 15 years old as it was my favourite game at that time. However, like most Master of Orion fans, I was very disappointed by Master of Orion 3 and I was quite skeptical about this. Thankfuly it has turned out to be a very good game despite its flaws.
UI: The UI in my opinion is where this game excels compared to the competition. Even a screenshot comparison between master of orion, galactic civilizations and stellaris shows that master of orion has the superior UI. There is clarity, everything fits nicely and it really feels like a game instead of a spreadsheet (a drawback of many other 4x games).
Races: Top voice acting by many famous Sci-fi characters, including Star Trek's Mr Worf and Q and Star Wars' Luke Skywalker. Nicely designed animations, vibrant graphics bring the races to life. The only drawback is that the number of races is relatively limited, however, it is being expanded with DLCs.
Tactical combat: There was a big debate whether this should have been realtime or turn-based. In the end the developers went for realtime and I have to say it works surprisingly well. Don't be fooled, it is not just a pretty cut scene where you sit back and watch ships destroy each other. Your actions really matter. I have tested this thoroughly. Even in battles where the auto-resolve feature or the AI control had me lose severely, I managed to win but it wasn't easy. Even tiny changes in ship trajectories can make a difference in battle. So, save, experiment and reload!
No Hall of Fame: Given that each game lasts dozens of hours to complete it is a shame to see that once you win and you return to the main menu it is over. There is no way to see a list of past game scores or victory types. I can't see how they didn't think of implementing this given that it is very basic for 4x games (master of orion 2, civilization and galactic civilizations have it).
Tedious mid-game: There are no rally points. There are no governors. "Autobuild" builds almost everything, even buildings you don't really need. There are not many exciting events happening in mid-game to keep your interest. Perhaps more random events or encounters should be added to address this. (Update: After the Antares patch, things have been far more interesting.)
AI: The AI is not bad, but it is not good either. At normal difficulty I don't feel that the AI poses a challenge. You can always outsmart it and sometimes it makes odd decisions, like moving huge powerful fleets away from the point where they need it the most. I believe the AI should be more aggressive in pursuing victory conditions.
Bugs: There are some minor, not game-breaking bugs in the game. Also some important tooltips (e.g. those about victory conditions details) are not working from time to time.
Hopefuly bugs, AI and omissions will be corrected or improved in future patches as the developers seem devoted to making this game a success. Despite its flaws, at its current low price Master of Orion is a bargain, it is fun and it is hard not to suggest this to any space strategy fan.

Personal Rating: 8.5/10
Pros:
1. This game allows some good role-playing elements and creative character builds.
2. The perk system is easy to follow and encourages you to make choices between great perks.
3. There is an incredibly awesome and active mod community on Nexus Mods which enhances the game greatly.
4. The dead space that was in Fallout 3 and New Vegas is fixed in this game with the Commonwealth. I loved those two games, but if I did a review on those two that would be one of my only cons. It makes sense why the dead space was there, but makes for a kind of boring area of the map. Fallout 4 doesn't have that problem at all. Especially with great mods.
5. The first DLC, Far Harbor, was a fun DLC with lovable and hateable people/factions.
6. You'll see that I will hate on the faction system in the game a little when it comes up against the story, but one redeeming quality is that there (SPOILERS?) isn't necessarily a bad guy when you think about it. Everyone has a reason for doing what they're doing but it just seems to clash with other peoples' desires/objectives. Makes choices hard in the first play through.
7. It's not like completing the game once is good enough. The game has GREAT replay value.
8. Despite the story being kind of sorta okay, everything else with side quests, settlements, NPC interactions, etc. is very fun and worth constant playthroughs.
9. Settlement building gives you the creative/creation element to the game and it feels great. Mods from Nexus Mods really amplify this in a huge way.
Cons:
1. BUGSSSSSSSSS. Sooooo many bugs. Some can be game breaking. There are mods that fix this, but something like that shouldn't be necessary.
2. The story... just isn't all that captivating for me. I didn't really have a desire to go find my son after the first play through. Same thought with Fallout 3. New Vegas did captivating story telling SOOO well. Wish Bethesda would have picked up on it.
3. The base game factions are okay... but fail in comparison to Fallout New Vegas. (may not be fair to compare games like this, but when a small developer does your game better than you it's necessary lol)

I liked the art style and the ability to change the direction of the storyline by your actions; different endings/playthroughs are always good, and you can tell the creator(s) put a lot of creative energy into this game.
However, it still doesn't qualify as a good game for three main reasons: 1) it's got a poor plot, 2) it has terrible game mechanics, and most important of all: 3) it is nowhere near balanced.
1) The Plot (Spoiler Alert)
The plot is unique, but so is any illogical story. It just doesn't add up. The Hero was never an actor, and yet this WHOLE time during acting, never actually hurt the main character (you)? Only when the main character gets confused does the hero suddenly actually become "what he's always been"? The plot is too forced, and just doesn't make any sense, and it's never resolved even by end game.
2) Game Mechanics
All of your abilities are trash, they do no damage. BUT if you and your ally copycat, then they are ehh ok. Here's the kicker: you and your ally have to copycat each other SEQUENTIALLY. That means if an enemy goes before you or your ally, the deal is off. Oh, and you tend to be the slowest character, while your ally is the fastest, so good luck syncing up. Also, your ally seems to randomize their moves, so good luck expecting them to copycat you. Oh, and if you're trying to copycat them and get the chance to go right after them- nope you're not in the clear yet because now you have to consider that your skills cost energy whereas hers don't, so you probably couldn't copy her even if you wanted to.
Not to mention, why copy your ally? If copying your ally is the only way to really impact the fight, then are you really playing a game, or watching a movie? Players make decisions to win games, they outwit their enemies. This pigeonhole game design doesn't allow for truly playing the game.
3) Game Balance
In case you're wondering how the game seems possible, it's because depending on the path you choose to follow, the game is easier. For example, play the bad guy and if you end up fighting Ralph, it's actually impossible. He has multiple abilities that one-shot you, (and of course, you cannot increase your health or any stat or even anything for that matter in ANY WAY ALL GAME). Mid-game you can use Darkness to pretty much beat anything, and your ally is actually useless by comparison.
Basically, when not in Darkness, your abilities suck. When in Darkness, they're OP and you don't even care what your ally is doing or even if they die. The whole copycat game mechanic integral to outmaneuvering the enemy goes completely in the trashcan with Darkness, but even that is hopeless against Ralph who literally one-shots and permastuns you. Of course, you don't have to fight him if you choose to be the good guy, which is another example of pigeonholing and poor game design/balance.
______

There's a lot of great potential for this game, although at its current state it's very sloppy. The FOV slider past 90 is actually the Ctulhu slider and the melee is super weird. Other gripes too such as no tutorial, clipping through teammate models and smaller gripes such as being able to look around while you're repairing holes in your ship.
It's very fun when things are going well and you're running a tight ship. There is a very exciting tension in the air when the captain tells you to get ready dockside and you are aiming your cannon waiting for the enemy ship.
Communication makes or breaks this game. The community will be an important part of keeping this game alive.
Without voice comms, the ship can get quite troublesome to deal with. As a captain, you don't know if your gunners think you should angle the ship. As a crew, you need to tell your captain what you need as well. As an experience, Blackwake will heavily rely on player communication.
Unfortunately the game at the moment doesn't have that much content other than straight ticket-based 'DM' PvP. There are hats though so Dota 2 fans will feel right at home. The shocking female pirate customization is game-breaking though (only 1 hairstyle??)
When you pretty much know all there is to do as a pirate, the flow can feel a bit too chore-y. Hopefully future patches will add more content and things to manage. This problem isn't as pronounced when playing as a captain, but in a TDM 3v3 game, only 6 out of roughly 60 people will play as captain.
The point of this game is that the fight to sink each other's ships will create many tasks for your crew to manage and coordinate. Naturally, the game gets quite boring when you have a terrible captain or are stomping the enemy so hard because they don't know how to play.

I have mixed feelings about this game.
This game is a short experience with no "meaningful" gameplay, just exploring the room and listening to the main character's memories. I actually have no problem with this, it's a nice half-hour of entertainment for the price of absolutely nothing. However there's something that hindered my experience. You see, this game has "over 40 contributors providing their wit and talents" according to its description. What does this mean? It means that while you're immersed in the game's depressive story you find a shelf with lots of books which titles break the fourth wall and/or reference their authors. While you're searching for memories of Serena in her dressing table, you find a postcard advertising the developer's new game in one of its drawers. These completely unhidden "Easter Eggs" completely ruin the immersion, like everyone wanted to put their "graffiti" in the game. Even the two paintings on the wall, which are actually quite creppy, are also contributions that don't really have nothing to do with the game's story.
About the story of the game, I didn't find the abrupt ending to justify all the tension the game had while listening to the memories about the furniture. There's actually nothing so scary to consider this an horror game, apart from the obvious plot twist at the end.
Do I recommend this game? Considering the game is a free, half-hour experience I don't see why not to try it for yourself. Would this game be worth paying if it was a premium experience? That would be more difficult to say. In the end, the game is more like a proof-of-concept of what the developer is capable of,  rather than a solid game on its own.

This game is very reminiscent of the other entries in the franchise, with a few notable differences:
Combat:
Squadmates can (And oftentimes do) die. This is often infuriating when you lose lots of progress on a squad member because of RNG, which leads to the immense desire to save after every turn.
The action camera is quite good. It's quite fun watching your character lob grenades from a perspective other than isometric.
The combat difficult, even on the lower difficulty settings.
Story:
It's very cliche, you're a rebel faction taking down aliens that have already conquered earth.
Other Gameplay:
This game features the familiar "Base building" that was also in other entires in the franchise, with notable differences. The resources this game forces you to manage are numerous, and the game does a very♥♥♥♥♥♥poor job of explaining most of them.
The mission system is just as bad, lots of missions are time-locked, and dissapear if not completed. This is all made the more frustrating by the fact that the game is constantly pushing you towards the end-game quests (Read: No leisurely gameplay here, the game forces you to take story missions, which can mean losing your chance to do other types of missions that might expire during the time it takes you to complete the story mission.) I suppose this lends itself to replayability, but it's not worth it in my opinion, and it's one of this games biggest failings.
TL:DR
This game is a solid game, it's a fun time sink if you've got nothing better to do. But as an XCOM game it falls flat, and tries to re-invent a series that didn't need reinventing, leading to a clunky UI, frustratingly busy gameplay, and irritating squad death mechanics that will leave series veterans frustrated.

Where do I start with Trove? Apparently they just updated it, but this review will be from when I've played it in the past. I took a bit of a scan of the new gameplay and it does not seem much different aside from a new class and a new biome.
Ultra kidfriendly MMO for people who like Minecraft, except it takes a lot of the fun out of what Minecraft had going for it.
Essentially the game comes down to endless, endless grinding. Grinding to a fault. You can't just "advance", you need to achieve shadow levels which you're either going to pay a hefty sum for, or grind until your eyes bleed. I got to shadow level 36 before I couldn't take the mindless repetition.
This game is ALL about the mindless, easy, boring grind. As I said before, it is kid friendly, but it lacks depth. All characters only have a couple abilities, no talent trees. Certain classes benefit from different attributes but that's baseline stuff in any RPG or pseudo RPG. And we're back to grinding, grinding, and grinding some more for just a little nudge toward upgrading that gear. That's how you advance, by the way, upgrading your gear. You're capped at a certain level, but your gear score adds some bonus levels for higher dungeons.
The shadow lairs are easy with the right group, and the boss tactics are predictable and unchallenging. The dungeons are all "random" in a way, but you can tell where the main "guy" is in every dungeon after playing for a few hours. You'll soon just say forget the trash mobs and skip right to the end. Actually, that IS what they do, when you run in "raid groups"... Which is basically, well--- you get into a world with a bunch of others, and clear a certain number of dungeons in a certain time period (based on whatever biome it tells you) and you get a reward. It's just mindless hip hopping from one "boss" to another in each dungeon as fast as possible. After about the 100th time of doing this, I just said to hell with it. It was unengaging, unimaginative, and yes, the recurring theme, BORING.
The server lag can be unbearable at times. Causing you to clip out and there have been instances where I did not get a drop, or did not get the dungeon-clear, or the boss glitches. There aren't a lot of bugs that I've found in the game, but these are pretty big ones.
I guess it's P2W, because you can buy your way into "mystery boxes" and either sell them, or open them yourself. Granted, you may not uncover anything good, but enough people have to where the game is not exactly fair to people who grind and can't get any RNG luck.
What the game essentially comes down to is collecting. Collecting mounts, pets, armor/weapon pieces (cosmetics), blocks. But once you hit max level, and collected everything you wanted to, what's the point? There's no real point in collecting anything, no achievement of any sort, besides the "hey look what I got" aspect. The "End Game" is pretty dull and lackluster. You'll just be relegated to mindlessly (there it is again) clearing dungeons and selling stuff for the heck of it.
There aren't many positives but a few of them are kind of neat. One cool thing about Trove is they use content creator's works and add it into the game. You can customize the way your character looks with new and fantastical voxel creations by many other players. The club worlds are also cool, and you can see a lot of creative stuff (from anime, to musical rides, to recognizable characters recreated, to just about anything one could imagine).
This voxel MMO is severly lacking in any real depth, but it does not have to. The graphics, art style, simplicty of gameplay mechanics appeal to the younger child bracket. Compare that to a MMO with a LOT of depth and interesting, more in-depth mechanicslike FFXIV. It's like comparing Heroes of the Storm to Dota2. One is very casual and easy to pick up, the other is hard to play effectively and brutal for newbies. Overall, it was fun for a couple days worth of gameplay, but not much else once you realize, well, there is NOT much else.

You came here for a review? I don't have one... Instead here is how to make an apple pie!
This easy apple crumble recipe proves that you don't have to buy one readymade, it's so simple to make your own - and it tastes much better! Simply layer fruit with a little sugar and a crunchy topping - this recipe uses oats but you can leave them out if you want a plain crumble - and bake. It's that simple! Now for the important question - custard or ice cream? This classic crumble recipe serves 6-8 people so if perfect if you're feeding big crowds. This delicious apple crumble will take you 35 mins in total. A homemade apple crumble is the perfect way to finish of a Sunday roast with the family.
Ingredients:
>900g (2lb) Bramley apples, peeled, cored and sliced
>75g (3oz) caster sugar
>1 tsp ground cinnamon
>For the apple crumble:
>175g (6oz) butter
>225g (8oz) plain flour
>100g (4oz) demarara sugar
>175g (6oz) jumbo oats
Method:
>Preheat the oven to 200°C/400ºF/Gas Mark 6.
>Place the apple slices, caster sugar and cinnamon into a large ovenproof dish.
>Rub the butter into the plain flour, sugar and oats.
>Scatter the crumble over the apple mixture in an even layer.
>Bake for 30-35 mins or until golden and the apples are tender.
>Serve your warm apple crumble with cream or ice-cream for a treat.

Sadly, I must now join that crowd, because I found Bastion to be a fulfilling Action RPG experience, without being able to really put my finger on exactly what drew me in. I'm not sure whether to recommend this or not, but after completing the main story (may continue on with the Dead Kings DLC and report on that, but considering how much of a struggle the main story was, I kind of don't want to), I'm leaning towards not recommending.
I'm sure we all know about how disastrous the PC and console launches for this game were. Ubisoft were
ambitious with their updated AnvilNext engine (which they have since further refined) that they ended up going way above the max amount of drawcalls for the DX11 API, leading to major performance issues, and just general lack of polish. It's still not great, but it's an improvement. Framerates were not great on my system - the difference between low and ultra (excluding antialiasing and Nvidia GameWorks settings, those are
the only graphics options that affect performance in Assassin's Creed Unity) is virtually nonexistent in terms of performance, so I just ran most of my settings at Ultra except for shadows, AO, and antialiasing. My average hovered around 50 FPS (45 is where I tend to draw the line), however I saw drops into the 30s and even 20s during my playthrough, albeit not very often. The menus often felt laggy and unresponsive as well.
Gameplay is very frustrating if you get detected, which for me was fairly often. Stealthing missions was a struggle, and the combat when you get detected is only really manageable if you're handling one or two enemies at a time. I've heard people tell me the Unity combat is "easy," which is absolute ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Maybe I'm just bad, but come on, how the♥♥♥♥♥♥is this easy?
Story is also fairly weak,
If you do plan to pick up Unity, get this on sale. I don't regret my purchase, but I would not pay more than $15. Thankfully, it was barely over $10 when I purchased. Assassin's Creed Syndicate has a similarly weak story, but at least that has not totally ♥♥♥♥ing frustrating gameplay to back it up.
RATING: 3/10

ARE YOU READY TO RUMBLE IN THE BLOOD BOWL?! Blood Bowl is a combination of a tactical and sports game developed by Cyanide Studios and published by Focus Home Interactive. The basics are extremely simple: two teams, one ball. The team that carries the ball into the opponent's end zone scores a touchdown, the team with the most touchdowns at the end of the game is the winner. However, it’s how you decide to do this that makes things interesting, the ends justify the means! It’s not just the players you have at your disposal either. You can bribe the referee to look the other way as you cripple or trample annoying opponents and hire illegal wizards to give you a hand directly from the crowd… Blood Bowl severely tests the finest tacticians' strategies.
Now, does the game deliver? At first, I was totally skeptical on recieving a tactical sports game, which I had never experienced before playing Blood Bowl, because I had never played one. Fortunately, it's a great game and delivers on the spot. The game is very fun to play as you use your players to travel to the end zone and hopefully not get squashed by the other team. And, you will be squashed, even through your diligent efforts. No matter what difficulty, you will experience challenges including turnovers, bribed referees (which is hilarious), and wizards deciding to mess up your good play.
The graphics in this game are...well...it was published in 2010, so you know what I mean. Even though it was published in '10, the graphics are still solid. It is nice to see some gigantic orcs facing the puny humans in a standoff, with some great textures. Even using low settings during the game, the textures function well as well as character models, which is great to see from a game as we don't see it much anymore.
How about controls and fluency? The controls are very easy to learn, once again thanks to the tutorial. Also, if you play strategy games, you should recognize controls right away because they're fairly simple to learn. The game is also very fluent with everything going on. The textures of the stadium and with the crowd, are pleasing. The AI is excellent and will 95% match whatever skill you're at, whether it's easy, medium, or hard, some mode will challenge you.
This game will mainly interest either sports or strategy fans the most, but that doesn't mean it isn't for you, because it's a great game for everyone. It's tutorial is great in everyway and I wish more game developers as were creative and descriptive, as Cyanide Studios was, with tutorials. As someone unfamiliar with the past of Masters of Orion and a newcomer to the series, I have to say that I've really enjoyed what I've played so far. It's basically Civilization in space, with very colorful and distinct races, exploration/combat/tech trees.
The main distinction is the overlying goal to reach Orion, a legendary planet populated by an advanced race. Other goals for victory are the typical ones we're used to..Diplomacy/Combat/Economy.
What struck me about the game is the amount of polish that went into it..I honestly had no idea Wargaming was developing this title and they've done a fantastic job fleshing out the world and giving distinct flavor to each race. Some are more keen to combat, others are more predisposed to economy, while a few are downright unpredictable and unstable.
The art and animation is fantastic. They even went so far as to add fully fleshed out space battles you can manually control with cinematic angles (Although auto resolve will be the solution 95% of the time). The dialogue with the races is really cool, and having to keep in mind the nuances of each race versus the planets you colonize also gives the game depth I haven't encountered before.
I've been having fun with it so far, but I do wish there was some campaign element. However, I've had a ton of fun creating my own narratives as my empires have prospered (And crumbled mostly) in this colorful scifi strategy title. Highly recommended.

Don't buy this game unless you enjoy being addicted.
I am about 50 hours in and I assume still a way to go - and I love it.
The game consists of a squad based, turn based strategic action within quite a few varied maps and in between you have the sort of hollywood based cut scenes that develop the story. Something I first saw in the old Dune and Command and Conquer games. XCOM 2 does this very well.
The story is well told and there is a lot of background detail that sucked me right in. The graphics, sound effects and music are top notch and they all remind me of military action films such as Transformers and GI Joe.
You are the main character from the previous game liberated from stasis. Time has passed and humanity lost the war against the alien scum - pfft.
As the 'Commander' you will manage a team of 4-6 soldiers and direct them through various maps that either reveal more of the overall story or simply to obtain resources to build your mobile base. Or in other terms - increase mankinds chance of surviving. The resources themselves are numerous. We have intel and supplies, scientists and engineers. We also have bits of alien corpses and technology. All of this stuff can further develop your own research and engineering goals.
Your base consists of a large mobile alien ship where your scientists can research and unlock new alien technology and the engineers can build stuff. YOU DECIDE what to research. YOU DECIDE what to build. YOU DECIDE whether to build a lab or a power relay. Whether to build a training complex to improve your squad or whether to build a specialist facility to research the secret alien tech. Base management on its own is quite an undertaking and it will take a while to understand the mistakes you will make.
The comms room in your base has an map overlay of the world where you can take on missions or attempt to contact the resistance based in other continents. There you will find a scary bright red line - like a doomsday clock - counting down to what - who knows - I crapped my pants. Halfway through the game with the doomsday clock nearly indicating the end of the world and missions being thrown your way left, right and centre - it will surely test your mettle.
DON'T PANIC!
At one point it will all come together and you will be forever playing the eternal balancing act. More intel or more supplies. Build a tower or travel to South Africa to pick up a scientist. One hundred other things to consider as well. It's an amazing joy ride and a huge rushhhhhhh.
Your squad are a bunch of nobodies but for some reason you get quite attached to them and start caring. They can be customised so like me you can have your demolition experts kitted out in bright red. The first member that became major I gave them a cigar. Unfortuantely they can get injured and therefore you need about 12 soliders in total. At least. As they complete missions they gain experience and skills. Interestingly enough my specialists seem to be the best characters so far, interesting becasuse their skill tree involves hacking computers and killer robots.
The mission section of the game is without equal in my experience. Simply stupendous. Expertly balanced so that it seems to me I just have enough time to stop the bomb detonating or just about to signal for the rescue ship when the alien scum send in another horde.
Remember in every action film the bomb ticks down to three seconds left before you stop it? This sort of thing happens quite often.
It's addictive as chips.
In many missions I just can't believe I made it through. It's very rewarding and often I have thought a mission was impossible before an hour later - I make it a huge success. Part of this is learning about skills and equipment and about cover. About timing.
Think about the A-Team and I LOVE IT WHEN A PLAN COMES TOGETHER.
FANTASTIC. I LOVE IT.
There is a lovely variety of alien scum to meet, shoot to pieces, take their brains back to base and research their♥♥♥♥♥ Makes me wonder why other developers can't do this.
XCOM 2 is even more complex than I can describe - do you want some?
50 hours in and about four crashes.
There is a lot of save scumming.
Some interface problems.
Many things not explained.
I did the advent forge mission. There are a lot of alien scum and a huge tech beast with enourmous power and armour.
I disabled it with my tech guy whilst the others killed its friends. When the monstrosity came back around I threw a mimic so its attention was drawn elsewhere. Meanwhile my whole squad hot ironed it with everything they had.
Call me Colonel Azlan.
AND I LOVE IT WHEN A PLAN COMES TOGETHER.

In MOO3 you would design ships to fit rolls in fleets including specialized point defense ships, bombers carriers, scout fleets (since the battle field was large enough that you would have to scout out enemy ships.)
The tech tree was interesting in MOO3 because each play through you would get different techs you wouldn’t get auto fire, enveloping, miniaturization,  on every weapon you would work with what you had and strategically trade for what you wanted.
MOO3 had a real economic, population growth simulator not little guys you drop around 3 choices.  ( MOO has some differnce in techs with each playthrough just not the extend of MOO3 and not in weapon mods.)
I don’t find the great voice acting adds to the game, the click of the klakons or beeps of the meklar conveyed just as much and gave them real personality instead of everyone speaking English.
MOO3 had horrible game breaking bugs, but its scope was amazing, the creativity you could use with ship and fleet design.  The real difference in weapon functions including ranges optimal damage range accuracy fire rate for point defense was so much more interesting.
In this MOO I have had the enemy ship AI go straight across the battlefield tell they hit the “wall” and just stop they didn’t even rotate to aim their front facing weapons at me multiple times. ( I have also had a couple combat freezes and large fleet battle lags)
all and all MOO3 with vanilla or strawberry mod >= MOO.

You are greeted by the gruff voice of a stranger. A voice that will be your guide, your mind and your comfort for the next six hours. You play the character of an unnamed Kid, who's job is to protect himself and other survivors from the aftermath of a calamity, and make ends meet on The Bastion: your safe haven. To do this you have to collect cores from the various locations around The Bastion and return them.
During gameplay you look down upon The Kid and fend off enemies' attacks. You can improve your weapons back at The Bastion and the narrator will comment on your progress.
The voice of the narrator and the soundtrack are the two things that bring the game from fun to brilliant. “Windbags ain’t much different than normal folks,” the narrator says as you crush one of the game’s enemies with your hammer. “All they want is a place to stay and a decent meal.” This makes smashing them that much harder. As for the soundtrack, it suits the mood perfectly; the whole experience drips with passionate artistry.
If you are thinking of buying this game, you have no idea what you are getting into. You will come to know of the beauty of Bastion, but you shall never understand it.

Finished the game, here's up and downs,
+A lot of sidequests, assasinations, collectibles
+Huge map where you can free run/jump as your heart's content
+Nice graphics, minimal fps drops on my computer (high end)
-Good story but there are a lot of gaps in telling it, quite predictable ending
-A MASSIVE AMOUNT of sidequests, assasinations, collectibles (that gets repetitive after a while)
Now the two big points that makes me not recommend the game:
-Game is hard and i mean not the kind of "rewarding" hard, it's the "annoying" hard. If you're a completionist like me, you want the complete all assasinations and heists and multiplayer quests right? Anything for the achievements. But even if you finish the storyline (which is required for strong gear) and upgrade yourself to top gear, you can still get ONE SHOT from snipers. The random guards and brutes are too powerful as well. I'm not a fan of earlier AC combat where 1 vs 50 is no problem, but this is annoying. This makes you play the side quests over and over again and gets pretty frustrating for a while. I don't want to plan every heist mission like it's the final boss assasination, i want to have fun (which i can't at the moment)
-I'm an AC fan and played all the games. This game struck me with the graphics....That's it, everything else was meh. Main character was likeable but not a legend. Story with a stroke of forbidden love was an original idea, but it felt uncomplete (because when you see two lovers only seeing each other from mission to mission you just can't feel the emotion. The game tells you they're in love but doesn't show you). Free run is allrightish, there is a %50 chance you go to where you like. Honestly after 49 hours i want to complete the game %100 percent but it feels like a job now.
So buy it on sale, because i'm not recommending the game on full price

TL;DR For a dollar with trading cards, it's an almost decent hack 'n' slash. What I feel are poor mechanics sour the experience. The devs absolutely learned from the mistakes in X-Blades and made Blades of Time a great game. Get BoT instead.
EDIT: Art direction is lovely but to say succinctly what I did in a rambling way: Blades of Time is fun. X-Blades really isn't.
I care not for anime sexuality.
I bought this game.
*GASP* How can that be?!
X-Blades is the predecessor to Blades of Time; Blades of Time is a remake/reimagining of X-Blades. I got BoT in a bundle. I very much enjoyed it. I bought X-Blades in the hopes of encouraging the dev's to include Cards for BoT / Achievements for X-Blades.
I did not fully grasp the significance of "reimagining." X-Blades is horrible when compared to Blades of Time. My saying so is unfair, of course, but also truth.
With X-Blades, I was hoping to relive the glory days of PS2 platformers (Sly Cooper, Jak & Daxter, Ratchet & Clank, Beyond Good & Evil, KyA, Vex, etc. etc.). LOL upon further research, X-Blades was released for the subsequent generation... so my hopes were dashed from the start.
Several reviews compare X-Blades to Devil May Cry; I'm pretty sure I compared BoT to DMC. X-Blades is similar to DMC only superficially: the targeting and combo system, the sword/gun-play, the double-jump, the fact that you fall slower while shooting, and of course the monsters (are vaguely similar). Other than that, X-Blades is a hodgepodge of (bad) mechanics.
You're a nimble nearly nude female treasure hunting... n-nin... er s-samur... er anime. Yeah.
You can swing your blades and shoot the shooty-things with the quickness; you can run (in the classic "back-bent-at-a-45-degree-angle-for-speed-and-style" pose) LIKE a ninja. When it comes to being swarmed by enemies... Ayumi moves like Zero from BoT: heavy and slow, tank-like.
I'm playing with a controller and I don't even know how to dodge; I got the Teleport power, but you can only use it when your feet are planted firmly on the ground. There is no manual lock-on to enemies; moving the camera over enemies does it automatically. This makes targeting the bosses amidst the throngs of grunts a chore. The Store Page doesn't mention controller support; you can play with a controller but there are no options like Right Stick or Vibration Sensitivity (I THINK you can remap buttons but IDK).
Speaking of mobs, you best get that Teleport power early on and refrain from jumping like you'd figure the agile MILF with a baby's face (yeah...) should be able to. Else, you'll float atop the mobs or, somehow, one of the grunts will end up on top of you, out of reach of your blades.
Combos... I don't even know. I don't even know how the points work, actually.
Your melee attacks are the only thing that multiply your combo; if you use guns or powers, you get nothing.
In BoT, you could run all over the map with the (pretty much useless) points ("souls," I think) following you tirelessly - you were never going to lose any of them. In X-Blades it seems if you get too far from the points, they just disappear.
If you're working on a mob, of course, the multiplier is multiplied. I think if you get hit once, you lose every bit of those banked points, rather than it just resetting to zero and getting the points you had earned. I like this idea, it is, how you say, "hardcore." When you can't maneuver well enough on your own to preserve that combo, when there isn't a block/parry; other reviews that say "The game is nothing more than spamming LMB" are correct. I hate to admit that, since that could be argued for SEVERAL games, but with X-Blades, it's absolutely true.
There is a bit of a prologue and you end up being sent to some other... dimension. The beach you spawn on is apparently a hub(?). I cleared the waves upon waves of enemies, went through the door that opened, cleared the boss and those waves, didn't find another door, went back through the first, back on the beach, cleared those waves, didn't find another door, went back through the first door, and had enough.
I'm certain some sorts of new mechanics / gimmicks will be employed throughout the game but I'm not sure I have the fortitude to deal with the just plain poor combat (which is, no doubt, the entirety of the game); monotony.
Get Blades of Time; it is fantastic (though Ayumi is (")a bit more(") conservative).

I recommend this game because it is one of my personal favorite survival games.  It most definitely demonstrates what surviving against other people and zombies in a huge open world map would be like.
One of the things that really stuck out to me is the fact that you get GREAT FPS, almost no lag whatsoever.  I own DayZ Standalone as well as this, and comparing the two, I've found that the Mod runs so much smoother.  I don't have the best computer, but that just proves my point even more since my computer can still handle the Mod.  And I'm not just saying I get no lag on the lowest settings, I can run the game on the highest video settings possible and it still runs as if I was playing Minecraft on the lowest settings, now that's damn good.
The gameplay is extremely good for being a mod.  The mod proposes fair fights for survival against other players, as well as surviving against the environment despite other people arguing against this just because they died too many times.  I enjoy every minute of the game, even when I die.  To me dying in this game just means a brand new start and a chance to get even better gear.  You definitely learn what to do and what not to do.  The game has concequences for your actions as if you were really in a zombie apocalypse, and that just adds to the fact that the game is almost as realistic as you can get.
My favorite thing on this game is the size of the map.  It's just huge.  Plain and simple.  You never run out of places to go and boredom is hard to achieve.  The size of cities/towns are acceptable, and the distance between them proposes that "journey" aspect that we all love about free roam.
Lastly, the game proposes a challenge.  Zombies are a ♥♥♥♥♥ in the beginning, but once you get weapons and such, you have bigger problems to prepare for.  Sickness, starvation, dehydration and other people.  You always have something to worry about, and that just makes the definition of survival even more present in this game.  It is survival of the fittest, and if you're not good enough, you WILL die.  That just means you have to adapt and learn to become the character you're playing as.
Of course I do have a few things that I dislike that I feel like I should share with readers.
-The inventory system isn't that great, It's really complicated.  I had a very hard time getting used to it, but after a while I had it down.
-Zombie AI blows, it's very hard to melee or shoot a zombie if you're not good at shooting targets that jerk back and forth or do unexpected things such as run away.
-The amount of controls you have to learn and master is insane.  But once again, once you learn, you don't forget.
-There are so many buildings that you wish you could go into, but you can't.  Cities are made up of a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of houses, and other structures but a good number of them are just decoration unfortunately.  This was quite annoying to me.
-If you are just starting out, it is a real pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to try outrunning zombies if you don't have a weapon of some sort.
These cons are most definitely outweighed by the pros.  Watching a tutorial will help with some of these such as the control and inventory problems as well as finding ways to get past zeds when you're a fresh spawn.
In conclusion, I reccomend this game for people who love a good free roam apocalyptic PVP survival game with a good challenge.  BUY IT! it's worth it!

I have to admit I was a skeptic when following the development of this game. As a fan of the classics I was worried about the direction this project was heading in, but after picking it up and playing it for a few hours I have to admit I am pleasantly surprised and enjoying myself quite a bit.
I enjoy all kinds of space 4x games, from MOO2 to Stellaris to Endless Space to Distant Worlds to Stardrive to... you get the idea. This game may not be as "complex" as some of those I mentioned, but what it focuses on it does quite well. Incredibly strong presentation and a smooth UI make the game feel easy to grasp and fun to play. Late game colony management can be a drag, but I find I have plenty of fun playing on smaller maps. The AI seems quite competent too, which isn't always the case in most space 4x games. I can see myself coming back to this game over and over to have some fun and get a taste of that "just one more time" feeling I love about this genre so much. If you are looking for a good entry point to space 4x games, or you just want to have some fun, I say pick this game up.
*Note that I actually like star lanes, at least the way they are implemented here, and the real-time combat offers enough control for me to enjoy it as well, but I understand those things can be show stoppers for some people.

12 Labors of Hercules is a nice relaxing game, personally I played it every day 30 minutes before going to work on a PC. The game is also available in a mobile form.
Do not think that the game is tedious and boring, absolutely not, we have a large map on which Hercules (the main character) and his helpers, ie Pegasus, Cerberus, Cyclops and Medusa, move.
In this game we collect supplies of food and building materials from which we build sawmills, farms and warehouses needed to produce raw materials and collect them.
Each level presents us with various challenges such as finding a hidden piece of the puzzle, completing the level at a given time.
The creators offered us various bonuses to facilitate the passage of a given level in the so-called "Golden Time", we have bonuses such as: fast building, fast moving, horn abundance (doubles the number of items to collect) additional employee and stop time in the hourglass.
We also meet several beasts from Greek mythology.
On each map there are various obstacles ahead of us, for example, we repair bridges and roads, we "patch" holes to unlock access to new heroes or resources of raw materials and places to build farm buildings.
There is a great diversity in terms of levels and opponents or our helpers.
I definitely recommend the game because I played great.
Advantages:
Heroes and beasts from Greek myths
A variety of beings and levels.
Very nice and pleasant graphics.
Pleasant music
A great time killer.
Disadvantages:
Short.
In summary, I recommend it as an excellent time killer who does not irritate.

I didn't really know what this game was about when I first purchased. I mean, I've seen the graphics and some of the gameplay footage, and since the price was so attractive, I decided to give it a go. Well, but what is it about?
You take control over Hercules, his minions and also some other mythical creatures, and you need to fulfill certain goals in order to advance to the next level. There's a time limit going on, which has a direct influence on your score, and throughout the way you can also unlock some special powers that will provide you some assistance during your quest.
There's not really much of a story, I mean, it's nothing complex and I think it suits this premise really well, after all, we're talking about a casual game. The graphics are nice, the sound effects are ok, the soundtrack gets boring after a while, but at least for me it didn't make much difference, as I was usually focused on what I had to do on each level. As for the gameplay, I'd say that it's a blend of strategy and management, as you need to build improvements and also collect resources along the way.
The game itself isn't very difficult, you can surely unlock every single achievement available without having a headache. Anyway, if you decide to give this game a try, I only advise you to take it easy, as binging can turn your experience into something really tedious.
Overall, it's a fun game and if you enjoy it, there're some other titles of this series available here on Steam for a very affordable price.

Assassin's Creed Unity offers a more enhanced experience to new and veteran AC players. Sadly, some of which needs improvement, especially the problems that were present during launch.
The game had a bad launch. I was expecting it to have a more polished release, but Ubisoft decided to release the game because they had a deadline to catch up. A lot of players gave a really negative impression on the game and the company as well because of numerous bugs and glitches that were present during release. I pre-ordered the game five months before its release because I was hyped for it and I'm also a hardcore AC fan. It was so disappointing that the game was half-baked, so I decided to refund it when Valve added refund systems on Steam.
After nearly two/three years, I decided to give this game a chance and bought it when it went on sale last week. I already finished the single player campaign, and I can say that the whole story of Unity is pretty forgettable in my opinion. Still, it's a pretty fun game to play. The Dead Kings DLC is pretty boring and annoying, especially when you explore the ruins. Pretty much you'll be surrounded by numerous thugs and probably end up dead in minutes. Multiplayer is fun as well. I tried two multiplayer missions and it's really cool that you get to complete missions with other players with different play styles. I'm glad that Ubisoft really did fix most of the bugs and glitches, and they also gave the Dead Kings DLC for free, which was supposedly be available for those who pre-ordered the game or purchased the season pass.
Here's a breakdown of my Pros and Cons of the game:
PROS
+ beautiful graphics
+ parkour is more improved and really fluid
+ multiplayer is fun
+ a lot of side quests
+ music is good
+ most bugs and glitches fixed
+ combat is easy and looks really cool, especially the finishers
+ stealth is improved
+ story is okay
+ you can choose skills and buy equipment that fit your play style
+ Paris is fun to explore
+ Weapons are really good
+ Dead Kings DLC can help you grind more money, especially when you loot chests
CONS
- controls are really annoying. I can't perform double-assassinations easily even if two enemies are close and whenever I free-run, sometimes I go the wrong way even if I'm facing a certain direction.
- AI is sometimes overpowered. They react easily even if you sneak.
- you cannot complete all skills even if you finish the single player campaign. You can earn more points for it on multiplayer.
- story is really short and forgettable, and you can finish it maybe in a few days
- a companion app may be required if you want to grind a lot. You can also pay for a premium upgrade if you want a "full experience"
- the characters speak English with a British accent instead of a French accent. It really ruins the immersion in my opinion (at least the crowd speaks French).
In its current state, I recommend you buy this game when it's on sale. I feel the current price may not be worth its value, but the game is really fun to play, especially with friends on multiplayer.
P.S. I guess this is my first "serious" game review. I still need to work on my composition, but I tried. :D

Do you like gambling? Do you like American football? Do you like fantasy creatures? Well, Blood Bowl combines all three of these things (dice from gambling, a ruleset based on American football, and teams of creatures from the fantasy Warhammer universe) and turns it into a board game. Blood Bowl Chaos Edition is the most complete digital version of the Blood Bowl board game to date.
Almost all of the dice rolling is hidden from the player (unless the player chooses to see it), leaving the player with only the fun choices: what team to play, and then who will be on that team and how they will play. The only dice you'll have to "touch" (ie, interact with), are the block dice, which randomly offer you a set number of possible outcomes of unit vs unit interactions based on the strength values of your units (you should really look up the mechanics of Blood Bowl if you want specifics; they're too in depth for me to go into here).
However, dice rolling is central to Blood Bowl, so even if you try to ignore it, it will always be there. And, between random events like where the fans come on to the field and knock out half your players and the inevitable moment when one of your players dies, there will be nothing you can do about it. No matter how great your tactical planning or how immense your foe appears, a single dice roll can turn the tide and usually does...in theory.
There are "bad" teams, meaning you will have a lot of problems if you chose them, and will likely lose. Even if you find a decent team that you want to play, you may have to work harder than you'd expect to play they how they're "supposed" to be played. There's a "cheating" system that will give you money if you go up agianst higher ranked teams, but there will often be times when the cheats you can afford are simply not good enough. If one of your players gets injured and is forced to miss the next game, you'll be stuck with a mercinary that is always worse than the player it replaces thatnks to a trait called "Loner." If one of your players dies, it's gone forever.
All of this culminates in a game that feels extremely punishing when you lose and is easy to become addicted to. You may have fun with it, but in my hours of play I rarely did. The dice rolling sucked away over 20 hours of my life, and it wasn't worth it. Avoid unless you love chance-based games.

This isn't helped by the fact that the first portion of X-Blades is spent working your way through arenas in the light of day, then turning around working your way back through those arenas in the evening. It's a serious copout on the part of the developers to not create new architecture and instead relight the same areas. A copout that should not go unnoticed.
What's Good:
- The game offers a nice challenge
- Does a great job at encourging a variety of approaches in battle
- Plenty of upgrades to purchase
- Rewarding collectibles
- Good variety gunplay
- The heavy role magic plays in combat
What's Not-So-Good:
- Battles can be repetitive
- Lack of variety in music
- Uneven difficulty in boss battles (ridiculously easy final boss)
- A few visual errors
What's Bad:
- Overly sensitive movement controls - ^ Unresponsive aerial movements
- Very poor storytelling
- ZERO character development
- Pointless levels
- Penatlizing players for buying life refills with very little alternatives
- Lack of variety in sword combo
In all, there are certain aspects of X-blades that are well developed while there are many others that are not. Depending on your level of tolerance, it can be a decent experience.
18 years later, and still the playability of this game never wavers. A true classic.
